title: 'Bursa dibuka tinggi pada pagi ini
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR,. Bursa Malaysia dibuka tinggi pada Selasa, seiring dengan momentum positif Wall Street semalaman, memandangkan harga minyak yang terkawal susulan pemulihan eksport minyak mentah dari Asia Barat, mengimbangi trend penjualan berterusan dalam pasaran bon Perbendaharaan AS. Pada 9.10 pagi, FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) meningkat 7.14 mata atau 0.44 peratus kepada 1,638.89 berbanding paras 1,631.75 ketika ditutup pada Isnin. Indeks utama itu dibuka 4.63 mata lebih tinggi kepada 1,636.38. Sentimen pasaran secara keseluruhan positif dengan kaunter untung mengatasi kaunter rugi sebanyak 272 berbanding 202, sebanyak 364 kaunter tidak berubah, 1,944 tidak diniagakan dan 13 digantung dagangan. Jumlah dagangan berjumlah 440.19 juta saham bernilai RM164.76 juta. Malacca Securities Sdn Bhd memaklumkan bahawa prestasi positif Wall Street semalaman menyaksikan Dow Jones Industrial Average, S&P 500 dan Nasdaq Composite masing-masing meningkat sebanyak 0.2 peratus, 0.7 peratus dan 1.1 peratus, manakala harga minyak mentah Brent dan hasil Perbendaharaan 10 tahun masing-masing mencecah US$100.3 setong dan 5.3 peratus. “Di peringkat tempatan, kami menjangkakan pelabur akan terus bersikap selektif menjelang pengumuman Belanjawan 2027, dengan tumpuan diberikan kepada sektor-sektor yang berpotensi mendapat manfaat. “Syarikat-syarikat dalam sektor mekanikal dan elektrikal mungkin terus menyaksikan minat belian, disokong oleh penekanan kerajaan terhadap infrastruktur kecerdasan buatan (AI) serta projek tulang belakang Grid Nasional 500-kilovolt Tenaga Nasional Bhd, yang memberi kelebihan kepada syarikat seperti MN Holdings Bhd, Southern Cable Group Bhd dan Powerwell Holdings Bhd,” menurut firma itu dalam nota penyelidikan hari ini. Selain itu, Malacca Securities menyatakan bahawa usaha mengurangkan air tanpa hasil (NRW) juga mungkin kekal menjadi tumpuan, berpotensi memberi manfaat kepada syarikat seperti ISF Group Bhd dan Ranhill Utilities Bhd. “Akhir sekali, 99 Speed Mart Retail mungkin menyaksikan minat belian baharu susulan jangkaan peruntukan bantuan pengguna lebih tinggi di bawah Sumbangan Asas Rahmah dan Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah,” menurut kenyataan itu. Sementara itu, Naib Presiden Penyelidikan Ekuiti Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd, Thong Pak Leng berkata Wall Street ditutup lebih kukuh, dengan Nasdaq mencatatkan paras tertinggi baharu apabila pedagang memilih untuk tidak mempedulikan cabaran pasaran semasa dan sebaliknya menumpukan perhatian kepada saham berkaitan AI bagi mengimbangi kesan kenaikan hasil bon. “Untuk hari ini, kami menjangkakan indeks akan bergerak dalam julat 1,630-1,640 memandangkan pasaran saham tempatan mungkin bersedia untuk aktiviti pembelian saham pada harga rendah,” katanya kepada Bernama. Saham berwajaran tinggi menyaksikan Maybank dan Tenaga Nasional naik empat sen masing-masing kepada RM10.04 dan RM13.04, CIMB menokok tiga sen kepada RM7.76, IHH Healthcare menambah dua sen kepada RM7.78, manakala Public Bank tidak berubah pada RM4.71. Bagi saham aktif, Zetrix AI melonjak setengah sen kepada tujuh sen, Divfex naik satu sen kepada 16.5 sen, Ramssol meningkat 2.5 sen kepada 86 sen, manakala SLGC yang baru disenaraikan di Pasaran ACE susut 3.5 sen kepada 24.5 sen, dan Dagang NeXchange merosot sentengah sen kepada 50 sen. Antara saham paling untung, Batu Kawan meningkat RM1.24 sen kepada RM20.22, Nestle dan Kuala Lumpur Kepong menokok 20 sen masing-masing kepada RM90.20 dan RM21.06, Petronas Dagangan melonjak 18 sen kepada RM19.38, dan Genting Plantations menambah 16 sen kepada RM5.82. HeiTech Padu mendahului saham rugi, susut tujuh sen kepada 88 sen, Thong Guan Industries, Sunway Construction Group dan Allianz Malaysia merosot enam sen masing-masing kepada RM1.44, RM7.55 dan RM20.74, dan UMS Integration menguncup empat sen kepada RM9.36. Di papan indeks, Indeks FBM Mid 70 bagaimanapun naik 41.29 mata kepada 17,584.78, Indeks FBM Emas meningkat 44.30 mata kepada 12,234.65, Indeks FBM Top 100 menokok 46.09 mata kepada 12,019.47, Indeks FBM Emas Syariah bertambah 39.24 mata kepada 12,108.25, manakala Indeks FBM ACE melonjak 7.73 mata kepada 5,614.34. Mengikut sektor, Indeks Produk dan Perkhidmatan Perindustrian naik 0.16 mata kepada 179.13, Indeks Tenaga meningkat 1.78 mata kepada 831.72, Indeks Perkhidmatan Kewangan melonjak 56.47 mata kepada 19,196.61, manakala Indeks Perladangan naik 73.78 mata kepada 9,004.81. — BERNAMA

title: 'Wealth
body: 'This article first appeared in Wealth, The Edge Malaysia Weekly on September 28, 2026 - October 4, 2026  Two veterans of Malaysia’s start-up and investment ecosystem — entrepreneur and investor Sivapalan Vivekarajah and former Pitch Platforms Sdn Bhd (pitchIN) chief operating officer Xelia Tong — are launching a RM50 million debut venture fund.  Main Market-listed automotive replacement-parts manufacturer New Hoong Fatt Holdings Bhd (NHF) (KL: NHFATT) has committed up to RM20 million as its anchor limited partner.  The investment will be made through its wholly owned subsidiary Jhi Soon Manufacturing Industries Sdn Bhd, which will subscribe for up to 20 million Class A redeemable preference shares in Cypress Drive Ventures at RM1 each, NHF said in a filing with Bursa Malaysia.  Cypress Drive Ventures is the first fund managed by Cypress Asia Sdn Bhd, which was founded by Sivapalan and Tong. It will target technology-driven local businesses at the pre-Series A and Series A stages that are profitable or have a clear path to profitability.  Cypress Asia is seeking the remaining RM30 million from family offices and other investors.  Investments will range from RM1 million to RM3 million per company. Cypress Asia expects to make five to seven investments initially and build a concentrated portfolio of 10 to 12 companies if the fund reaches its RM50 million target. Depending on the deal, it may lead the round, co-invest with another fund or join an existing group of investors.  The fund has a seven-year term, with the option of two successive one-year extensions.  Cypress Asia expects to make its first investment in the first quarter of 2027. It plans to hold its first investment committee meeting in November and already has a pipeline of potential deals that will undergo due diligence.  The pipeline will draw on the co-founders’ existing networks, including companies from accelerator ScaleUp Malaysia’s portfolio and Sivapalan’s Soonicorn Collective for later-stage technology businesses as well as businesses within the network Tong built at pitchIN, a digital fundraising and investment platform.  Sivapalan and Tong worked together at ScaleUp Malaysia, as a senior partner and a managing partner respectively. They invested in 38 companies under the initiative.  Sivapalan also launched the Soonicorn Collective’s Titan, a 12-month coaching and execution programme for founders seeking to scale their business towards RM100 million in revenue, in which 18 businesses took part.  “We have a network of companies that we can invest in. Because we’ve been in the ecosystem for so long, people trust us,” says Sivapalan, co-managing partner of Cypress Asia.  The firm will also source investments through equity crowdfunding platforms and other venture capital firms.  The fund is sector-agnostic but will invest only in technology-driven businesses, says Tong, CEO and managing partner of Cypress Asia. Potential areas include electrical and electronics, automotive, digital health and agriculture.  “There are certain areas that we don’t touch — highly regulated businesses, those very dependent on state government contracts, businesses that are purely software, such as human resources software, or very e-commerce-driven. Other than that, we’re quite open,” she says.  Cypress Asia will look for companies that can grow profitably and reach a listing or acquisition without having to raise money repeatedly. Tong says an investee should ideally need no more than one or two additional funding rounds after Cypress Asia’s investment.  “Our investment thesis is to look for companies that already have a profitable business. It doesn’t have to be a lot; it can be a small profit, or at least they should be profitable this year. But they must be able to prove to us that they can be profitable,” says Sivapalan.  “We want to take them to RM8 million to RM10 million in profit over a five-year period and then list them on Bursa Malaysia or another exchange. The good thing about getting them to profitability is that they also become interesting for a merger and acquisition, so it serves a dual purpose.”  Endorsement from a public listed company  NHF became Cypress Drive Ventures’ anchor investor after about 2½ years of discussions with Tong, as the automotive-parts group explored ways to gain exposure to innovation and diversify its sources of income.  Tong first came to know the family behind the company through business and start-up networks when she was at Cradle Fund Sdn Bhd. She had previously encouraged a family member involved in running the group to set up a corporate venture capital arm but the proposal was too early for it at the time.  The proposal was subsequently presented to NHF’s board of directors two or three times, with the board raising extensive questions as the company was new to venture investing. Tong says the process gave both sides time to understand what they were entering into and helped build trust.  Initially, NHF committed RM10 million. When Cypress Asia decided to apply for Jelawang Capital’s Emerging Fund Managers’ Programme at the end of 2024, NHF raised it to RM12 million, which was the amount of private capital Cypress Asia needed to meet the programme’s 20% threshold for a fund of at least RM60 million.  In the end, Cypress Asia was not selected for the programme but Tong says NHF proceeded with the investment as its decision was based on the managers’ experience rather than the prospect of matching capital. It later increased its commitment to RM20 million.  “We are blessed to have them as our first and anchor investor. They genuinely want to look at the innovation side of things and potentially diversify into other businesses,” says Tong.  For NHF, the fund offers potential financial returns and exposure to businesses and technologies beyond its existing network.  Tong also sees the commitment as an example of how cash held by profitable listed companies can be put to work in Malaysia’s venture ecosystem.  “I think Securities Commission Malaysia has also always been trying to get more private pockets to actually invest in this space, to make investments in venture funds … A lot of companies, especially listed ones, are sitting on a lot of cash, but it is a lazy balance sheet that is not doing anything for the business,” she says.  Sivapalan adds: “[NHF] is a main board company, and they are willing to take a chance with us. It gives other people the confidence that they can also take a chance with us.”  Experienced investors  Sivapalan and Tong say their previous investments and years spent working with founders will shape how they manage the fund.  “We have been through the mill. We did not just come out of corporate finance and decide to do this. We have worked with many founders,” he says.  Sivapalan has spent close to four decades as an entrepreneur, coach and angel investor. He has personally invested in 16 businesses as an angel investor and also co-founded ScaleUp Malaysia, as well as founded the Soonicorn Collective.  Tong had investment roles at Malaysia Debt Ventures Bhd and Cradle Fund, where she was vice-president of investment and headed the Angel Tax Incentive programme. She later became a managing partner at ScaleUp Malaysia and, most recently, chief operating officer of equity crowdfunding platform pitchIN.  Both see the venture fund as a continuation of their earlier work. During ScaleUp Malaysia’s first three years, investments were made at a fixed valuation of RM2.5 million. Sivapalan says some stronger companies wanted ScaleUp as an investor but eventually declined its offer as the valuation was deemed too low.  A venture fund gives Cypress Asia more flexibility to invest in such companies at a later stage and at valuations that reflect their growth.  “After running an accelerator, the natural progression is to move into a venture capital fund. An accelerator cannot offer different valuations to different companies, so we lost those opportunities … Then Xelia said there might be a corporate investor, and Jelawang came along. So, we thought, ‘Let’s give it a try. Let’s try to raise the fund.’”  Sivapalan adds that the broader aim is to rebuild confidence in Malaysia’s venture capital industry. “There is very low trust in the VC industry today … If the VC industry cannot prove itself, then you can’t raise money to support start-ups and help them grow.  “The VC model can work, and I think we would like to show that we have the right insights, the right model and the right thinking to make this work.”

title: 'Bursa opens in the green — then heavyweight selling takes over
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 — Bursa Malaysia opened higher on Wednesday but retreated shortly after, weighed down by selling activity in selected heavyweight counters, led by financial services and industrial products and services. At 9.11am, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) eased 3.68 points to 1,629.67 from Tuesday’s close of 1,633.35. The index opened 0.19 points higher at 1,633.54. However, on the broader market, gainers outpaced decliners 221 to 180, with 306 counters unchanged, 2,083 untraded and 13 suspended. Turnover stood at 327.37 million units worth RM150.56 million. Hong Leong Bank eased 10 sen to RM21.98, CIMB slid 15 sen to RM7.55, and Press Metal Aluminium fell six sen to RM7.13. These three counters collectively pulled down the composite index by a combined 7.23 points. Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd vice-president of equity research Thong Pak Leng noted that Wall Street maintained its positive momentum overnight, with the S&P 500 testing an intra-day record high underpinned by a tech-inspired rally. “This is despite the US 10-year yield remaining elevated at 5.286 per cent while Brent stayed above the US$100 per barrel mark. Over in Hong Kong, the Hang Seng Index maintained its uptrend, underpinned by renewed interest in tech-related stocks as sentiment recovered amid the steadying crude oil prices,” he told Bernama. Back home, Thong said he is anticipating bargain-hunting activities to emerge, although any upside may be hampered by selling from foreign funds following the FBM KLCI’s mildly positive close yesterday. “In view of this, we expect the index to continue consolidating within the 1,630-1,640 range today,” he added. Among other heavyweights, AMMB slipped five sen to RM6.42, Petronas Gas erased eight sen to RM17.20, and Mr D.I.Y. edged down one sen to RM1.24. IHH Healthcare added three sen to RM7.94, and Maybank gained two sen to RM9.99. In active trade, Top Glove gained 5.5 sen to 93 sen, and Supermax added 2.5 sen to 48.5 sen, while Zetrix AI and Ni Hsin inched down half a sen each to 8.5 sen and 37 sen, respectively. Metronic Global was flat at half a sen. Among the top gainers, Malaysian Pacific Industries jumped 62 sen to RM45.58, Nestle gained 32 sen to RM91.58, and Mi Technovation rallied 19 sen to RM6.19. title: 'Share price soars as earnings continue to shine
body: 'This article first appeared in The Edge Malaysia Weekly on October 5, 2026 - October 11, 2026 AMMB Holdings Bhd Once again, AMMB Holdings Bhd (KL:AMBANK) is taking home The Edge Billion Ringgit Club (BRC) award for Highest returns to shareholders over three years under the financial services category. Notably, its share price has climbed steadily over the last five years, with the most significant jump recorded between 2024 and 2025. The stock gained 41.9% from RM3.70 on March 31, 2024 to RM5.25 on March 28, 2025. Between March 28, 2025 and March 31, 2026, the banking group’s share price continued its upward trajectory, reaching RM6.59, before hitting another record high of RM7.37 on Aug 12. Much of the enthusiasm about the stock can be linked to the potential return of excess capital to shareholders, which could either come in the form of higher dividends or through other capital return initiatives. AMMB, under its five-year strategic plan called “Winning Together 2029” (WT29), aims to double its dividend per share by the financial year ending March 31, 2029 (FY2029) from 22.6 sen in FY2024. This would be supported by earnings growth and capital optimisation, with Basel 3.1 reforms providing a meaningful upside catalyst. AMMB has already been increasing its dividend payout ratio, from 40% to 50% in FY2025, exceeding its earlier dividend payout ratio guidance of 35% to 40%. Total dividends increased from 22.6 sen in FY2024 to 30.2 sen in FY2025 and 35 sen in FY2026. Its three-year compound annual growth rate for shareholder returns totalled 27.9% for the period between March 31, 2023 and March 31, 2026. The increase in dividends can also be attributed to the yearly improvements in earnings. In FY2026, the group achieved its highest-ever net profit of RM2.1 billion, 5% higher than the previous year’s RM2 billion, driven by both net interest income and non-interest income. Net profit was RM1.87 billion in FY2024. Net interest income rose 4.5% in FY2026, backed by higher margins, while non-interest income grew 5.1% mainly from trading gains. For FY2026, the bank recorded a return on equity (ROE) of 10%, in line with its guidance to analysts. The group’s ROE has stayed at 10% over the last three financial years. In the recent 1QFY2027 financial performance, AMMB’s net profit came in at RM520.23 million, up slightly from RM516.18 million in the previous year on account of improvement in net interest income growth. The earnings were within analyst expectations. Non-interest income grew 5.1% year on year, supported by stronger wealth management fee income but net interest income was softer, compressing to 1.93% in 1QFY2027 from 1.97% in 4QFY2026, as competitive asset pricing and funding mix pressures weighed on margins. CIMB Securities has downgraded its call on AMMB to “hold” with an unchanged target price of RM7.35, based on 1.09 times price-to-book value (PBV). “While we remain constructive on AMMB’s medium-term capital return and efficiency story, we believe the key rerating catalysts from its recent WT29 capital management update are largely priced in. The next catalyst, the Basel 3.1-driven capital release, remains some distance away given its implementation date of Jan 1, 2028,” said the research house in a report dated Aug 19. It added that while further rerating under the FY2028 valuation framework is possible, the rerating will need to be supported by earnings delivery rather than valuation roll-forward alone. Meanwhile, HLIB Research — which has kept its “buy” call on the stock for a target price of RM7.80 based on an implied 2027 PBV of 1.1 times — said its loan growth should remain firm going forward, led by mid-corporate and wholesale banking, adding that it should start contributing more meaningfully to non-interest income from 2QFY2027. Nonetheless, it also warned that the prolonged Middle East disruptions could create further stress among selected Business Banking accounts, although the management is expecting around half of the current stage 2 exposures to revert to stage 1 by September if logistics disruption normalises. HLIB Research added that the capital appreciation still has legs, “propelled by the plausible rerating catalyst of a potential RM2 billion capital return from FY2028”. It has estimated that the capital return could translate into a dividend yield of over 8.5% for 2028. Save by subscribing to us for your print and/or digital copy. title: 'Bursa Malaysia Extends Losses at Midday On Selling Pressure
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 – Bursa Malaysia continued its downward trend at midday on Thursday, October 1, 2026, as selling pressure persisted across the board, tracking mixed global market performance amid rising United States Treasury yields. Broader market sentiment remained negative, with decliners outpacing gainers 583 to 305, while 464 counters traded unchanged, 1,421 untraded, and 12 suspended. Half-day turnover stood at 1.65 billion shares valued at RM1.18 billion. Heavyweights and Active Stocks Major banking, utility, and healthcare blue chips pulled the benchmark index lower: - IHH Healthcare contracted 19 sen to RM7.64. - Maybank and Tenaga Nasional lost 6 sen each to RM9.93 and RM12.90, respectively. - CIMB decreased 5 sen to RM7.74. - Public Bank fell 4 sen to RM4.66. Among active counters, Zetrix AI and V.S Industry both added half a sen to 16.5 sen and 28.5 sen, respectively. Dagang Nexchange rose 1.5 sen to 50 sen, while Jaks Resources eased half a sen to 20 sen and ACE Market debutant GB Bond dropped 2.5 sen to 22.5 sen. Declining counters were led by Kuala Lumpur Kepong, which dropped 76 sen to RM21.44. Other notable pullbacks included Allianz Malaysia (down 62 sen to RM21.00), as well as Fraser & Neave, Hong Leong Industries, and Batu Kawan, which trimmed 42 sen each to RM21.32, RM16.04, and RM20.10, respectively. title: 'IOIPG Malaysia REIT to Pay Out Quarterly Dividends, List With Assets Worth RM7.66b
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 24): IOIPG Malaysia REIT is planning to pay out at least 90% of its distributable income on a quarterly basis, as the real estate investment trust seeks listing on the Main Market. The trust is listing with properties in Klang Valley and Penang worth RM7.66 billion combined, according to its draft prospectus. The trust also has the right-of-first-refusal to acquire local assets owned by its sponsor IOI Properties Group Bhd (KL:IOIPG). IOIPG Malaysia REIT will also consider assets of other owners though the priority will be retail, office, industrial and hospitality properties in urban and suburban areas in Malaysia. The proposed initial public offering (IPO) will allow IOI Properties Group to trim its debt from an acquisition spree involving over RM1 billion in 2024. The developer is also considering spinning off its Singapore properties worth RM26 billion into another real estate investment trust. The listing of IOIPG Malaysia REIT was approved by the Securities Commission last month and the target was to complete the listing before the year ends. The IPO will be split into retail and institutional tranches, offering up to 40% of the total issued fund size upon listing. Institutional investors, including cornerstone investors, will be allocated 27% of the total units. Cornerstone investors — typically large institutional investors such as pension funds and insurers — commit to taking up a portion of the IPO shares before they are marketed to other retail and institutional investors. Their presence helps to build up other investors’ confidence to invest in the IPO. Under the retail tranche, shareholders of IOI Properties Group are entitled to 10% of the units on offer on the basis of one unit for every 10 existing shares of the developer held on a date to be determined later. The Malaysian public will only be allocated 2%, while eligible persons under pink form allocation get up to 1% of total units. Net proceeds from the listing will accrue entirely to IOI Properties Group after covering estimated listing expenses totalling about RM4 million. Maybank Investment Bank and AmInvestment Bank are the joint principal advisers, global coordinators, bookrunners, managing underwriters and underwriters. DBS Bank is the joint global coordinator and joint bookrunner. CIMB Investment Bank, Hong Leong Investment Bank, RHB Investment Bank and UOB Kay Hian are the joint bookrunners and underwriters. Oversea-Chinese Banking Corp is also one of the bookrunners. title: 'SAMSUNG MALAYSIA AND MAYBANK PARTNER TO LAUNCH MALAYSIA’S FIRST SAMSUNG WALLET QR PAYMENT EXPERIENCE MalaysianUpdates
body: 'Kuala Lumpur, 24 July 2026 — Samsung Malaysia Electronics (SME) Sdn Bhd (Samsung) and Malayan Banking Berhad (Maybank) have entered into a strategic partnership to introduce Malaysia’s first Samsung Wallet QR Payment experience, marking a significant development in the country’s digital payments landscape. The collaboration, formalised through the signing of a Collaboration Agreement, combines Samsung’s mobile innovation with Maybank’s established digital banking ecosystem to provide Samsung Galaxy users with a faster, more seamless way to make everyday payments. Beginning 21 July 2026, eligible Samsung Galaxy users will be able to access Maybank’s MAE Scan & Pay functionality directly within Samsung Wallet through the latest application and software updates. As Malaysia continues its transition towards a cashless economy, the partnership reflects both companies’ commitment to making digital payments simpler, more secure and convenient for customers across urban and suburban communities. With QR Payment integrated directly into Samsung Wallet, users can quickly access the feature with a swipe before using Maybank’s Scan & Pay via the MAE app to complete their transactions. The integrated experience is designed to reduce unnecessary steps when making payments, whether users are purchasing meals, groceries, coffee or other everyday essentials. The QR payment functionality can also be used regionally across Singapore, Thailand, Indonesia and Cambodia, providing greater convenience for Samsung Galaxy users when making payments beyond Malaysia. President of Samsung Malaysia Electronics, Charles Kim, said the partnership with Maybank represents an important step in expanding the Samsung Wallet ecosystem in Malaysia. He added that integrating QR payments directly into Samsung Wallet is intended to make everyday transactions more effortless, allowing users to swipe, scan and pay within seconds. Meanwhile, Mohd Amri Mohd Sofian, Head of Community Financial Services Malaysia at Maybank, said the collaboration supports the Bank’s ROAR30 ambitions by focusing on intuitive digital experiences and frictionless payment journeys. Integrating MAE Scan & Pay directly into Samsung Wallet, he said, provides customers with greater convenience while maintaining the security and reliability associated with Maybank’s digital banking services. Beyond convenience, users can also earn Samsung Reward Points with every eligible transaction. These points can subsequently be used to purchase Samsung products or redeem vouchers available through the Samsung Members application, adding further value to everyday payments. As part of the partnership, Samsung and Maybank are also offering exclusive rewards worth up to RM500,000 through a limited-time promotional campaign running from 28 July to 30 October 2026. Eligible customers will receive RM5 after successfully connecting and activating QR Payment on Samsung Wallet, with the opportunity to enjoy up to RM15 in cashback or vouchers when they make qualifying purchases. The launch represents another milestone in Samsung’s efforts to expand Samsung Wallet beyond its existing capabilities and strengthen its role as a comprehensive digital platform for Galaxy users. By bringing together Samsung’s mobile ecosystem and Maybank’s digital banking infrastructure, the partnership aims to provide millions of customers with a more connected, convenient and efficient payment experience.

title: 'Anak syarikat ES Sunlogy tuntut RM1.17 juta daripada Ecolectric, Maybank terlibat prosiding garnisi | DagangNews - Berita Bisnes Anda
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR 2 Okt - Anak syarikat milik penuh ES Sunlogy Berhad, Savelite Engineering Sdn Bhd sedang mengambil tindakan untuk menguatkuasakan penghakiman mahkamah bernilai RM1.17 juta terhadap Ecolectric Engineering Sdn Bhd selepas Mahkamah Tinggi membenarkan prosiding garnisi melibatkan Malayan Banking Berhad (Maybank). Mahkamah Tinggi Kuala Lumpur membenarkan permohonan Savelite bagi Perintah Garnisi Tunjuk Sebab terhadap Maybank, yang dinamakan sebagai garnisi pertama Ecolectric, dalam pendengaran ex parte pada 30 September lalu, menurut pemakluman ES Sunlogy kepada Bursa Malaysia. Mahkamah menetapkan 21 Oktober 2026 bagi pendengaran tunjuk sebab. Perintah Garnisi atau Garnishee Order merupakan proses undang-undang yang membolehkan pihak yang memperoleh penghakiman mahkamah memohon mendapatkan bayaran daripada wang milik pihak yang berhutang di bawah penghakiman tetapi dipegang oleh pihak ketiga, seperti bank. Dalam kes ini, Maybank dinamakan sebagai garnisi dan perlu menunjukkan sebab kepada mahkamah sebelum mahkamah memutuskan sama ada wang yang mungkin dipegang bagi pihak Ecolectric boleh digunakan untuk memenuhi penghakiman tersebut. Savelite akan mendapatkan Perintah Garnisi Tunjuk Sebab itu dan mengatur penyerahannya kepada Maybank mengikut arahan mahkamah. Prosiding itu menyusuli penghakiman ingkar pembelaan yang direkodkan terhadap Ecolectric pada 17 Ogos 2026 berhubung pertikaian kerja pemasangan elektrik bagi projek pembangunan kediaman di Damansara Heights. Pertikaian projek Damansara Heights Menerusi penghakiman itu, Ecolectric diperintahkan membayar RM1,174,327.72 kepada Savelite dalam tempoh 14 hari. Jumlah itu merupakan RM1,234,551.27 yang diputuskan mahkamah selepas ditolak wang tahanan RM60,223.55 yang dipegang Savelite. Pertikaian itu berpunca daripada surat anugerah bernilai kira-kira RM1.65 juta bertarikh 25 April 2022, apabila Savelite melantik Ecolectric sebagai subkontraktor untuk membekalkan tenaga kerja bagi pemasangan perkhidmatan elektrik untuk projek pembangunan kediaman 54 unit di Damansara Heights. Savelite mendakwa Ecolectric gagal atau enggan menempatkan tenaga kerja yang mencukupi atau berkemahiran di tapak, menyebabkan kerja tidak dapat dilaksanakan mengikut program yang dipersetujui. Savelite memfailkan writ saman dan penyata tuntutan terhadap Ecolectric pada Julai 2026. Menurut pemakluman ES Sunlogy, Ecolectric tidak memasukkan kehadiran dalam tempoh 14 hari selepas writ saman dan penyata tuntutan diserahkan serta gagal memfail dan menyerahkan pembelaannya dalam tempoh ditetapkan. Mahkamah Tinggi kemudian merekodkan penghakiman ingkar pembelaan terhadap Ecolectric pada 17 Ogos 2026. Selain bayaran RM1.17 juta, mahkamah memerintahkan ganti rugi am ditaksir dan kos RM528 dibayar oleh Ecolectric kepada Savelite. ES Sunlogy sebelum ini berkata Savelite telah membuat rosot nilai penuh sebanyak RM3.17 juta ke atas jumlah terhutang daripada Ecolectric berkaitan projek Damansara Heights dan Old Klang Road, mencerminkan penilaian kumpulan terhadap kebolehkutipan jumlah tersebut. - DagangNews.com

title: 'Budget 2027 could deliver double relief for businesses, middle-income Malaysians - CIMB securities | Business | The Vibes
body: 'MALAYSIAN businesses and middle-income households could receive a double boost from Budget 2027 through wider sales and service tax (SST) exemptions and targeted personal income tax cuts, potentially easing operating and living costs, CIMB Securities says. CIMB Securities, in a research note, said there was scope to broaden SST exemptions for production-related inputs as businesses continued to face elevated energy, logistics and other operating costs. It expects further SST relief to reduce government collections by about RM1 billion, although underlying economic growth should still lift SST revenue by 5.5% to RM72 billion in 2027. Unlike the goods and services tax (GST), SST does not have a general input tax credit mechanism, meaning businesses can pay tax on inputs without being able to deduct it against tax charged on their own sales. This can result in tax costs being embedded throughout the supply chain, CIMB said. The research house expects extending selected exemptions to be the more immediate option in Budget 2027, while a broader input tax credit mechanism could be introduced from 2028 or later because of the additional administrative and refund framework required. For households, CIMB sees scope for targeted personal income tax relief for middle-income taxpayers, particularly those facing higher living costs but receiving less direct cash assistance. As an illustration, it said tax rates for chargeable income of RM50,001 to RM70,000 and RM70,001 to RM100,000 could each be reduced by one percentage point to 10% and 18%, respectively. The current 25% tax bracket could also be split, with a 24% rate applied to chargeable income between RM100,001 and RM150,000. Such a package could provide annual tax savings of RM200 for taxpayers with RM70,000 in chargeable income, RM500 at RM100,000 and up to RM1,000 for those with RM150,000 and above, CIMB estimated. It said the illustrative tax package would cost the government about RM800 million a year. More broadly, CIMB expects Budget 2027 to continue providing household support while maintaining fiscal consolidation, forecasting the fiscal deficit to narrow slightly to 3.4% of gross domestic product in 2027 from an estimated 3.5% in 2026. The research house also expects cash assistance under Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah to increase by RM2 billion to RM17 billion, supported partly by lower fuel subsidy spending. CIMB forecasts petrol and diesel subsidies to fall to RM32 billion in 2027 from RM41 billion, creating room for higher household assistance and development spending while keeping the government on its fiscal consolidation path. Budget 2027, the fifth Madani Budget and the second under the 13th Malaysia Plan, is scheduled to be tabled in Parliament on Oct 9. The Ministry of Finance has said the budget will focus on areas including cost-of-living pressures, business competitiveness and productivity while maintaining fiscal discipline.

title: 'HLIB Retail Research – Tradersbrief 23 Sep
body: 'Global. Asian markets ended mixed as investors weighed easing oil prices and bond yields against lingering geopolitical risks. Sentiment remained cautious ahead of the 23–25 Sep Trump-Xi meeting, with markets hoping for an extension of the US-China trade truce while watching developments on AI, export controls and rare-earth supplies. Meanwhile, Iran indicated it could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days if Washington eased military pressure, while Saudi Arabia reportedly restarted its East-West Pipeline, raising hopes of improving oil supply. Wall Street (Dow -0.36%, S&P 500 0.0%, Nasdaq 0.45%) ended mixed as continued AI strength offset weakness in financials, while easing oil prices and geopolitical tensions supported sentiment. AI infrastructure stocks remained in demand, fuelled by strong reception for Meta’s Muse AI agent. Meanwhile, Anthropic’s new lower-cost AI model added to optimism over broader AI adoption, with its reported IPO targeted for November. Geopolitical risks remained in focus as Trump said the US and Iran could reach a deal after the November midterm elections, while Tehran indicated it could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days if Washington eased military pressure. Malaysia. Tracking Wall Street gains, bargain-hunting in selected heavyweights and oversold readings, the KLCI jumped 16.6 pts to 1,683.5, led by IHH, CIMB, SUNWAY, HLBANK, PBBANK and MAYBANK. Market breadth improved to 1.48 from 1.18, while trading activity rose 5% to 3.58bn shares worth RM3.15bn. Foreign institutions (+RM20m; 5D: +RM75m; MTD: -RM674m; YTD: -RM5.13bn) and local retailers (+RM20m; 5D: +RM205m; MTD: +RM1.06bn; YTD: +RM0.62bn) were net buyers, while local institutions remained net sellers (-RM40m; 5D: -RM280m; MTD: -RM389m; YTD: +RM4.51bn). After a 95-pt surge from its YTD low of 1,655 on 29 Jun to 1,753 on 26 Aug, the KLCI corrected to 1,661.9 (21 Sep) before rebounding to 1,683.5 on 22 Sep, with momentum indicators turning up. However, the index remains below the LT ascending line and within the descending channel, keeping the near-term bias bearish, with major supports pegged at 1,655 (YTD low) and 1,639 (23.6% FR). On the upside, reclaiming 1,685 (50% FR) and 1,701 (MA200) would strengthen signs of stabilisation, targeting 1,717 (MA50) and 1,731 (76.4% FR). A decisive breakout above these levels would negate the bearish setup and refocus attention on 1,753 and 1,771 (YTD high). With expectations of a constructive Trump-Xi summit, easing oil prices and oversold technical readings, the KLCI could extend its rebound towards 1,700. However, the index remains entrenched in a downtrend channel, while tricky domestic backdrops—including potential 2H earnings disappointments amid a higher-for-longer cost environment, the dissolution of the Melaka state assembly today for the 16th state election, and lingering GE16 speculation—could cap gains and keep volatility elevated ahead of Budget 2027 on 9 Oct. title: 'A trader’s guide to navigating Budget 2027
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia’s consumer and construction stocks may emerge as beneficiaries of next year’s spending plan as Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim seeks to ease living costs while maintaining fiscal prudence. Anwar, who also serves as finance minister, is expected to announce measures to support households and sustain infrastructure spending when he unveils the annual budget on Friday. Investors will also be on watch for any update on a potential minimum-wage revision, which may boost consumption but add to earnings risk for companies. While Malaysia’s economy remains resilient, a renewed climb in oil prices is driving up fuel-subsidy costs, potentially weighing on the fiscal outlook and investor confidence. The spending plan ahead of a national election due early 2028 comes as Anwar seeks to rebuild public support following recent state poll setbacks. “Given the proximity to the 16th general election or GE16, this will be a people’s budget,” said Alexander Chia, analyst at RHB Research. “Social protection initiatives targeted at the lower and mid-income groups will be positive for the consumer, property, transport and healthcare sectors.” The country’s stock benchmark has fallen nearly 3% this year, lagging some South-East Asian peers including Thailand and Vietnam, as fiscal and political risks weigh. Moreover, foreign funds have sold US$1.59bil of local shares on a net basis so far in 2026. Several key areas warrant close attention in the Budget 2027 announcement. Budget 2027 is poised to include targeted assistance and measures to boost wages as the government seeks to temper the prospect of rising inflation on the cost of living. A likely increase in cash handouts to around RM17bil from RM15bil in 2026 should support mass-market consumption, according to Apex Securities analyst Wong Kai Heng. That should benefit retailers such as 99 Speed Mart Retail Holdings Bhd and Padini Holdings Bhd, as well as food and beverage companies including Nestle (Malaysia) Bhd, CCK Consolidated Holdings Bhd and Oriental Kopi Holdings Bhd. Analysts expect a modest increase in the development expenditure, which would provide continued support for infrastructure investment. Key projects that could feature under Budget 2027 include the light rail transit in Penang, the Northern Perak Water Supply Scheme and basic infrastructure projects in Sabah and Sarawak. “Potential beneficiaries of development expenditure expansion would be concentrated among contractors and suppliers exposed to water infrastructure and pipe replacement, flood mitigation, rural infrastructure, grid investment, and projects in Sabah and Sarawak,” Ivy Ng Lee Fang, an analyst at CIMB Securities, wrote in a report. That may boost firms in the construction industry, including Gamuda Bhd, IJM Corp Bhd and Malayan Cement Bhd. The government may allocate funds to upgrade the national grid and water infrastructure to support rising demand from data centres, according to Max Koh, an analyst at RHB Research. Greater funding, along with efforts under the National Energy Transition Roadmap, may benefit energy firms like YTL Power International Bhd and Tenaga Nasional Bhd. Meanwhile, Samaiden Group Bhd and Solarvest Holdings Bhd may also gain from new solar tenders. Investors in the bond market will be focused on the fiscal deficit target, as well as the debt supply for 2027 amid higher energy costs. Any further subsidies that could impact the government’s fiscal consolidation efforts may weigh on investor sentiment. “Prudent fiscal policy is increasingly appreciated by markets,” said Winson Phoon, head of fixed‑income research at Maybank Securities. “We expect further progress toward the government’s medium-term fiscal target of 3% of gross domestic product (GDP), potentially setting a target of 3.3% of GDP.” — Bloomberg

title: 'Mandat Pengurus Keselamatan Kebakaran Bomba bagi 9,451 Bangunan Tonjolkan Permintaan Pematuhan untuk Unique Fire
body: 'Langkah Malaysia menjadikan pemilik bangunan bertanggungjawab secara langsung terhadap keselamatan kebakaran dijangka meluaskan pasaran pematuhan bagi pembekal perlindungan kebakaran, sekali gus meletakkan Unique Fire Holdings Berhad (“Unique Fire”) antara syarikat yang berpotensi mendapat manfaat. Mulai 1 April 2027, pemilik 9,451 bangunan yang ditetapkan di bawah Akta Perkhidmatan Bomba akan diwajibkan melantik Pengurus Keselamatan Kebakaran (FSM) dan Pegawai Keselamatan Kebakaran (FSO), serta menubuhkan Organisasi Keselamatan Kebakaran (OKK) di premis masing-masing. Ketua Pengarah Jabatan Bomba dan Penyelamat Malaysia (JBPM), Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad berkata, keperluan itu selaras dengan Seksyen 27A Akta Perkhidmatan Bomba (Pindaan) 2025. Menurut beliau, mana-mana bangunan yang diperiksa dalam tempoh satu hingga dua tahun akan datang dan diwajibkan memiliki Perakuan Bomba perlu melaksanakan struktur baharu tersebut. Beliau berkata demikian selepas melancarkan program FSM dan FSO di Menara Merdeka Maybank, Kuala Lumpur pada 6 Oktober 2026, di mana kumpulan pertama seramai 174 FSM dan 324 FSO menerima sijil masing-masing. Perubahan utama melibatkan kaedah pembaharuan Perakuan Bomba. Selepas ini, JBPM akan menilai laporan pemeriksaan tahunan yang disediakan oleh FSM bagi tujuan pembaharuan perakuan, tanpa perlu menjalankan pemeriksaan fizikal ke atas setiap bangunan setiap tahun. JBPM kini mempunyai 13 penyedia latihan berdaftar dan telah mengeluarkan tender bagi menambah bilangan penyedia latihan serta jurulatih. Tanggungjawab pematuhan beralih kepada pemilik bangunan Rangka kerja ini memindahkan tanggungjawab keselamatan kebakaran harian daripada pihak berkuasa kepada pemilik bangunan dan kakitangan dalaman mereka yang bertauliah. Di bawah program ini, FSM menjalani kursus lima hari merangkumi pemeriksaan bangunan, perancangan pemindahan, pelaporan dan penyelenggaraan, manakala FSO menjalani kursus teknikal selama tiga hari. Dengan FSM bertanggungjawab ke atas laporan tahunan yang menjadi asas pembaharuan Perakuan Bomba, pemilik bangunan dijangka memberi penekanan lebih besar untuk memastikan alat pemadam api, gelung hos, pili bomba, sistem pemercik, peranti pengesan dan penggera serta sistem pemadaman kebakaran sentiasa berfungsi dengan baik. Ini menunjukkan permintaan yang lebih stabil bagi penggantian, penyelenggaraan dan pengisian semula peralatan di seluruh 9,451 premis yang ditetapkan, termasuk bangunan berpenghuni tinggi dan berisiko tinggi. Unique Fire, yang ditubuhkan pada 1997 dan beribu pejabat di Shah Alam, Selangor, terlibat dalam pemasangan, pembuatan dan pengedaran sistem, peralatan dan aksesori perlindungan kebakaran aktif untuk persekitaran terbina. Rangkaian produknya merangkumi alat pemadam api mudah alih, gelung hos, sistem pili bomba dan pemercik, sistem paip naik basah dan kering, peranti pengesan dan penggera kebakaran, serta sistem pemadaman kebakaran termasuk sistem kimia basah dan karbon dioksida. Kumpulan memasarkan produk di bawah jenama sendiri iaitu Unique, Unique227, Yama dan Commander, di samping jenama pihak ketiga seperti Kidde, serta menyediakan perkhidmatan penyelenggaraan peralatan perlindungan kebakaran dan mesin pengisian semula alat pemadam api kimia kering. Kumpulan telah pun mengenal pasti akta yang dipinda itu sebagai pemacu permintaan. Bagi tahun kewangan berakhir 31 Mac 2026, hasil Unique Fire meningkat 6.2% kepada RM114.7 juta, disokong oleh jualan pemasangan dan pengedaran yang lebih kukuh, terutamanya sistem pemadaman kebakaran. Pengarah Eksekutif, Marcus Liew berkata perniagaan teras perlindungan kebakaran terus berkembang dalam persekitaran kawal selia yang menyokong, dipacu oleh penguatkuasaan Akta Perkhidmatan Bomba (Pindaan) 2025 serta pelaksanaan projek di bawah Rancangan Malaysia Ketiga Belas, dan Kumpulan menjangkakan permintaan yang berterusan hasil keperluan pematuhan peraturan dan penganugerahan kontrak yang sedang berjalan. Kumpulan turut meluaskan jangkauan ke luar negara melalui Unique Mosafe Sdn Bhd, usaha sama 60:40 dengan Shanghai Mosafe Equipment Co Ltd untuk mengeluar dan membekalkan pemercik kebakaran, dengan Shanghai Mosafe menyediakan sokongan teknikal ke arah pensijilan Underwriters Laboratories (UL). Dengan keperluan FSM dan FSO berkuat kuasa dalam tempoh kurang enam bulan lagi, rejim pematuhan baharu ini dijangka mengubah keselamatan kebakaran daripada pemeriksaan sekali setahun kepada tanggungjawab berterusan bagi pemilik bangunan, satu peralihan yang selari dengan tawaran produk dan perkhidmatan Unique Fire.

Pengarah Eksekutif, Marcus Liew berkata perniagaan teras perlindungan kebakaran terus berkembang dalam persekitaran kawal selia yang menyokong, dipacu oleh penguatkuasaan Akta Perkhidmatan Bomba (Pindaan) 2025 serta pelaksanaan projek di bawah Rancangan Malaysia Ketiga Belas, dan Kumpulan menjangkakan permintaan yang berterusan hasil keperluan pematuhan peraturan dan penganugerahan kontrak yang sedang berjalan. Kumpulan turut meluaskan jangkauan ke luar negara melalui Unique Mosafe Sdn Bhd, usaha sama 60:40 dengan Shanghai Mosafe Equipment Co Ltd untuk mengeluar dan membekalkan pemercik kebakaran, dengan Shanghai Mosafe menyediakan sokongan teknikal ke arah pensijilan Underwriters Laboratories (UL). Dengan keperluan FSM dan FSO berkuat kuasa dalam tempoh kurang enam bulan lagi, rejim pematuhan baharu ini dijangka mengubah keselamatan kebakaran daripada pemeriksaan sekali setahun kepada tanggungjawab berterusan bagi pemilik bangunan, satu peralihan yang selari dengan tawaran produk dan perkhidmatan Unique Fire.

title: 'Sector Sweep - Singapore’s Maritime Sector Sees Stronger Earnings and Business Sentiment
body: '5 Maritime Stocks with the Highest ROE Source: Bloomberg and SGX data as of 30 September 2026. Rising offshore rates, sustained chartering demand and firm order books are lifting earnings across Singapore’s maritime sector. Clarksons Research reported that 2026 is on track to be a historically strong year for newbuild contracting, with 2,128 ships ordered in the year to date, double the ten-year average. The medium-term outlook also remains constructive, with maritime trade forecast to grow 2 per cent annually between 2026 and 2030. The top 10 maritime stocks by return on equity (ROE) recorded an average ROE of 24.4 per cent as at 30 September 2026. Outperformers include Yangzijiang Shipbuilding and small- and mid-cap names, such as Nam Cheong, Beng Kuang Marine, Marco Polo Marine, and ASL Marine Holdings. Yangzijiang Shipbuilding delivered a ROE of 32.2 per cent and a year-to-date total return of 54.5 per cent. The group reported record 1H2026 revenue of RMB17.5 billion, up 36.2 per cent year-on-year, and net profit growth of 28.4 per cent. Supported by higher-value vessel contracts and a favourable product mix, its order book stood at US$22.4 billion across 256 vessels, providing earnings visibility into 2030. Nam Cheong recorded the highest ROE among the group at 45.4 per cent, with net profit more than doubling on the back of contributions from both its shipbuilding and vessel chartering businesses. The company expects to add five vessels by year-end, while 71 per cent of its fleet is secured on long-term charters. In August 2026, RHB Research maintained its ‘Buy’ recommendation, citing its promising growth prospects as well as undemanding valuation. Growth is expected to be driven by a larger fleet of vessels, contribution from its new shipbuilding segment, and margin expansion from a more favourable sales mix. Beng Kuang Marine posted a ROE of 34.1 per cent as stronger engineering and shipbuilding activity lifted 1H2026 net profit by 20.8 per cent year-on-year. The group secured S$85.2 million in new contracts in the first half and ended June with S$70.7 million in outstanding contracted work. In August 2026, UOB Kay Hian maintained its ‘Buy’ recommendation and expects re-rating to continue due to the full consolidation of Asian Sealand Offshore and Marine which would provide a significant earnings uplift in 2H2026, alongside strength in its underlying business and market leadership. Marco Polo Marine achieved a ROE of 25.9 per cent and is seeking to unlock value from its shipyard business through the proposed reverse takeover of Fuji Offset Plates Manufacturing. The group is also expected to benefit from growth in offshore wind projects and continued fleet expansion. In September 2026, Maybank Research maintained its ‘Buy’ recommendation, noting that the group is entering a rapid-growth phase from FY26 to FY30 and will benefit from its diversification away from oil & gas into offshore wind projects, supporting energy-security concerns that have been underscored by the Iran–US conflict. ASL Marine more than doubled full-year net profit to S$33.3 million, driven by stronger chartering performance and lower finance costs. Its shipbuilding and chartering order books stood at approximately S$18 million and S$61 million respectively. Meanwhile, Seatrium continued its turnaround, recording a 54 per cent year-on-year increase in 1H2026 net profit (excluding divestment gains) and maintaining a net order book of S$13.3 billion. The group remains on track to achieve its FY2028 targets, including EBITDA of more than S$1.0 billion, as part of its efforts to enhance total shareholder returns. title: 'AHB kekalkan agihan pendapatan lima sen seunit bagi tahun kewangan 2026
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Amanah Hartanah Bumiputera (AHB) mengekalkan agihan pendapatan sebanyak lima sen seunit bagi tahun kewangan berakhir 30 Sept 2026, yang memberi manfaat kepada lebih 82,000 pemegang unit. Pelaburan Hartanah Bhd (PHB) bersama pengurus dananya, PHB Asset Management Bhd (PHBAM), berkata agihan pendapatan akhir bagi tempoh enam bulan berakhir 30 Sept 2026 adalah sebanyak 2.1 sen seunit, dengan tambahan agihan bonus sebanyak 0.4 sen seunit yang diisytiharkan PHB selaku penaja dana itu. “Edaran bonus itu akan diberikan bagi 1,000,000 unit pertama bagi setiap pemegang unit. Dengan mengambil kira agihan pendapatan interim sebanyak 2.5 sen seunit yang diisytiharkan pada April 2026, jumlah keseluruhan agihan pendapatan AHB bagi tahun kewangan berakhir 2026 adalah lima sen seunit,” menurut kenyataan itu. PHB berkata sebanyak RM120.13 juta akan diagihkan pada pusingan akhir, menjadikan jumlah keseluruhan agihan tahunan sebanyak RM236.41 juta. Pengarah Urusan kumpulan PHB Mazuki Abdullah @ Muhammad berkata agihan pendapatan bagi setahun penuh itu mencerminkan daya tahan AHB yang berterusan serta kekuatan portfolio hartanah asasnya, disokong pendekatan pengurusan aset dan pelaburan yang berdisiplin oleh PHB. “Prestasi AHB tahun ini membuktikan komitmen kami untuk terus memberikan pulangan yang kompetitif kepada pemegang unit. “Pada masa sama, kami kekal memberi tumpuan kepada usaha memperkukuh kedudukan AHB sebagai instrumen pelaburan pilihan pelabur Bumiputera menerusi pengurusan modal yang berhemat, strategi pelaburan yang dinamik serta pengoptimuman portfolio yang berterusan bagi memastikan pertumbuhan yang mampan danpenciptaan nilai jangka panjang,” katanya. Sementara itu, Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif PHBAM Zulkifli Ishak berkata pengurus dana itu kekal fokus menguruskan AHB secara bertanggungjawab bagi memastikan dana berkenaan terus menjadi pilihan pelaburan yang mudah diakses oleh pelabur Bumiputera. PHB berkata agihan pendapatan itu akan dibayar dalam bentuk unit AHB yang dikreditkan terus ke dalam akaun AHB pemegang unit selewat-lewatnya pada 13 Okt 2026. Agihan tersebut akan dilaburkan semula secara automatik, sekali gus membolehkan pemegang unit menambah pegangan unit serta berpotensi menikmati kesan pengkompaunan dalam jangka panjang. “Pelabur Bumiputera yang ingin melanggan AHB boleh berbuat demikian pada harga tetap RM1 seunit, dengan pelaburan minimum RM100 dan maksimum RM1 juta. “Langganan boleh dibuat melalui cawangan pengedar yang sah di seluruh negara, iaitu Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank), AmBank Bhd, AmBank Islamic Bhd, Bank Islam Malaysia Bhd dan Bank Kerjasama Rakyat Malaysia Bhd,” katanya. – BERNAMA

title: 'AG Cautions on Use of AI, Effective Human Oversight Is Still Essential
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): While the emergence of artificial intelligence (AI) has been used extensively and relied upon in the last few years, Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar cautioned for the need for human oversight in its usage. Dusuki said there is no doubt that AI offers significant opportunities in various sectors. For instance, he said, in healthcare, it can assist clinical judgement while in the corporate sphere, it can support decision-making, improve efficiency, and help professionals process increasingly complex information. “But as our reliance on these systems grows, so, too, does the importance of understanding how they are used and how they are governed. We need to ask some very practical questions: How reliable is the information produced by an AI system? What are the limits of its capabilities? Who is responsible for checking its output?” he said. He questioned what would happen when the AI system does not perform as expected. “These are not merely questions about technology. They are questions of governance, professional responsibility, and human oversight. Increasingly, they may also have consequences for legal liability and insurance. “For any institution adopting AI, it is therefore important to understand why the technology is being used, what risks may arise from its use, and what safeguards are necessary. Technology may assist professional judgement, but effective human oversight remains essential,” he reminded. Dusuki was delivering his keynote address at the Inaugural Financial Lines Forum at a hotel here. Also present were Lembaga Tabung Haji chairman and RHB Bank founder Tan Sri Abdul Rashid Hussin, who delivered a special address, and former Federal Court judge Tan Sri Zainun Ali, former Chief Judge of Malaya Tan Sri Hasnah Mohamed Hashim, as well as former and current judges. The AG said that while there are continuing issues in the usage of AI, there is a need to use it responsibly. Dusuki said the use of AI requires engagement among those who develop the technology, those who deploy it, those who rely on it, and those who assess and manage the risks associated with its use. Hence, he welcomed the organisation of such a forum like the Financial Lines forum as it brings together legal professionals, healthcare practitioners, corporate leaders, insurers, brokers, and other stakeholders. “We have an opportunity to learn from one another, to better understand the risks and opportunities before us, and to consider how our respective professions can respond responsibly to a rapidly changing environment. “Ultimately, the question is not simply what artificial intelligence can do. The more important question is, how we, as professionals, choose to use it responsibly,” he added. The one-day forum gathers medical experts, insurers, lawyers, and judges in exchanging views on medical negligence, governance, and AI. Meanwhile, in her welcoming address, Zainun, the chairperson for the Financial Lines forum, said a decision made in a boardroom may engage directors' duties, regulatory standards, disclosure obligations, and insurance coverage. “The adoption of AI in a hospital may raise questions of clinical judgement, patient safety, informed consent, data governance, institutional responsibility, and professional indemnity. “A claim may begin as a private dispute, but reveal a broader weakness in governance, documentation, communication, and risk management. No single profession has all the answers. Judges see how disputes crystallise and how legal principles operate in real cases. Regulators see patterns across institutions and markets. Lawyers advise on duties, responsibility, and remedy,” she said. Zainun added that directors and general counsel confront the practical demands of governance. “Doctors and hospital leaders carry responsibility for patient care. Insurers and reinsurers and brokers understand how emerging risks are assessed, transferred, and ultimately borne. “Sound risk management begins before a claim arises by identifying exposures, strengthening safeguards, and preparing for the consequences of loss. Risk professionals, insurers and reinsurers bring combined experience that can help institutions make informed decisions about the risks they accept, reduce, or transfer. The purpose of this forum is to place these perspectives in conversations with one another,” she said. The forum is organised by Messrs Chan Ban Eng & Co (CBE) where its managing partner, JJ Chan, is the founder of the Financial Lines forum. Chan said that he is pleased that Malaysia now has its own dedicated, pro bono Financial Lines forum, and he is proud to have founded it. “Financial Lines connects specialist questions of medical negligence, corporate and directors’ liability, insurance and reinsurance, and AI governance risk. Bringing these disciplines together can help improve patient care, strengthen governance, and deepen understanding of claims and coverage,” he added. title: 'Bursa Malaysia Edges Higher as Risk Appetite Improves - MCI Group
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — Bursa Malaysia closed slightly higher today, in line with upbeat regional markets, as improved risk appetite was supported by softer US labour data, that reduced expectations of further Federal Reserve tightening and eased pressure on bond yields. At 5pm, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) rose 0.88 of-a-point to 1,631.75 from last Friday’s close of 1,630.87. The benchmark index, which opened 2.55 points higher at 1,633.42, moved between 1,630.95 and 1,640.46 throughout the trading session. However, on the broader market, decliners surpassed gainers 599 to 564, while 523 counters were unchanged, 1,087 untraded and 24 suspended. Turnover improved to 4.78 billion units worth RM2.89 billion, compared with 4.23 billion units worth RM2.70 billion last Friday. Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd vice-president of equity research Thong Pak Leng said technology shares were among the main beneficiaries. On Wall Street overnight, the S&P 500 gained 0.73 per cent to 7,722.72 and the Nasdaq Composite rose 1.19 per cent to 27,190.86. For the local bourse, we remain slightly positive in the near term as the FBM KLCI remains in an oversold position following last week’s sharp correction, which should continue to attract bargain hunting, particularly in selected blue chips. “Domestic liquidity also remains supportive, with local institutions recorded RM352.4 million of net buying last week, although persistent foreign selling remains a headwind,” he told Bernama. Hence, Thong expects the benchmark index to stage a gradual recovery but remain volatile, with the FBM KLCI likely to trade within the 1,620-1,650 range this week. Among the heavyweights, Public Bank rose five sen to RM4.71, CIMB perked up eight sen to RM7.73, Tenaga Nasional climbed four sen to RM13.00, Maybank eased two sen to RM10.00, and IHH Healthcare slipped four sen to RM7.76. In active trade, V.S Industry rose three sen to 32 sen, Zetrix AI erased five sen to 6.5 sen, Jaks Resources inched down one sen to 17 sen, Excel Force MSC slid four sen to 17 sen, while NationGate was flat at RM1.83. Among the top gainers, Malaysian Pacific Industries increased RM1.00 to RM43.40, UMS Integration jumped 37 sen to RM9.40, Kelington garnered 49 sen to RM9.12, Nestle advanced 48 sen to RM90.00, and Samaiden surged 35 sen to RM3.19. Top losers were led by Batu Kawan, which decined RM1.48 to RM18.98; United Plantations fell 32 sen to RM31.06; Hengyuan Refining Company trimmed 18 sen to RM3.46, while Kuala Lumpur Kepong and YTL Power International shaved off 14 sen each to RM20.86 and RM5.54, respectively. title: 'Maybank falls below RM10 for first time in nine months, rising bond yields hurt banking stocks
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 1): Malayan Banking Bhd (KL:MAYBANK) fell below RM10 for the first time in nearly nine months and banking stocks mostly declined on Thursday amid rising bond yields. Higher yields generally hurt banks as they take larger paper losses from lower prices of the bonds they hold, which eats into capital and forces them to book losses if they sell. Banks will also have to increase their rates to attract depositors, leading to higher funding costs. That would weigh on banks’ near term non-interest income as well as their capital ratios, Affin Hwang Investment Bank flagged in a note on Thursday. Maybank, the country’s top bank in terms of assets, fell for the third straight day and closed down 0.4% at RM9.95. CIMB Group Holdings Bhd (KL:CIMB) and Hong Leong Bank Bhd (KL:HLBANK) each declined over 1%. The Bursa Malaysia Financial Services Index, which also tracks non-bank firms such as insurers and stockbrokers, fell to its lowest level in 10 months. The US Federal Reserve raised interest rates earlier this month for the first time in three years, sending the yield on the 10-year benchmark Malaysian Government Securities to as high as 4.18% before moderating. A growing number of economists expect Bank Negara Malaysia to raise the overnight policy rate in November during the final scheduled monetary policy review for the year. Rising yields tend to lead to higher corporate bond yields, which also tie-in to capital raising decisions both for banks and other corporates and, subsequently, fee income to the banks, Affin Hwang said. Maybank and Alliance Bank Malaysia Bhd (KL:ABMB) have on their books the longest bond duration — the length of time for a bond to repay its cost in cash flows while also being a measure of sensitivity to changes in interest rates — according to the research house’s analysis. Public Bank Bhd (KL:PBBANK) and Hong Leong Bank, meanwhile, have the shortest duration. In terms of capital ratios, Maybank, RHB Bank Bhd (KL:RHBBANK) and CIMB could see the largest drops, while Public Bank and Hong Leong Bank would see the least due to their portfolios’ shorter duration, the house added.

title: 'Bursa Malaysia dibuka tinggi, jejaki peningkatan di Wall Street
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR, 5 Oktober: Bursa Malaysia dibuka lebih tinggi pada Isnin, menjejaki kenaikan Wall Street berikutan pertumbuhan gaji Amerika Syarikat (AS) yang lebih perlahan, meredakan jangkaan kenaikan kadar faedah serta-merta oleh Rizab Persekutuan (Fed) AS. Pada 9.10 pagi, FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) meningkat 5.01 mata atau 0.31 peratus kepada 1,635.88 berbanding paras 1,630.87 ketika ditutup pada Jumaat. Indeks utama itu dibuka 2.55 mata lebih tinggi kepada 1,633.42. Sentimen pasaran secara keseluruhan positif dengan kaunter untung mengatasi kaunter rugi sebanyak 224 berbanding 158, sebanyak 337 kaunter tidak berubah, 2,054 tidak diniagakan dan 24 digantung dagangan. Jumlah dagangan berjumlah 206.30 juta saham bernilai RM98.78 juta. Naib Presiden Penyelidikan Ekuiti Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd, Thong Pak Leng berkata hasil bon 10 tahun AS kekal tinggi pada paras 5.28 peratus manakala harga minyak mentah Brent ditutup pada US$102.25 setong, menjadikan sentimen pasaran sensitif terhadap kadar faedah dan perkembangan di Asia Barat. “Di Hong Kong, Indeks Hang Seng susut di bawah paras 24,000 berikutan penyusutan saham sektor kewangan dan teknologi. “Di pasaran tempatan, susulan penutupan lebih tinggi FBM KLCI pada Jumaat lepas, kami menjangkakan kestabilan sementara dalam julat 1,625-1,635 hari ini, dengan aktiviti pembelian saham pada harga rendah memberikan sedikit sokongan di sebalik sentimen pasaran yang berhati-hati,” katanya kepada Bernama. Saham wajaran tinggi menyaksikan Maybank, Public Bank, CIMB dan Tenaga Nasional menambah empat sen masing-masing kepada RM10.06, RN4.70, RM7.69, dan RM13.00, manakala IHH Healthcare berkurangan enam sen kepada RM7.74. Bagi saham aktif, VS Industry menambah tiga sen kepada 32 sen, Notion VTec naik empat sen kepada 74.5 sen, GB Bond meningkat setengah sen kepada 23.5 sen, SFP Tech menokok satu sen kepada 28.5 sen, manakala Dagang NeXchange tidak berubah pada 51.5 sen. Antara saham paling untung, Samaiden naik 19 sen kepada RM3.03, UWC meningkat 16 sen kepada RM7.73, Critical Holdings menokok 15 sen kepada RM2.61, Mi Technovation melonjak sembilan sen kepada RM5.30, dan Solarvest mengukuh lapan sen kepada RM4.25. Nestle mendahului saham paling rugi, susut 32 sen to RM89.20, manakala Vitrox merosot 14 sen kepada RM10.32, Kobay Technology berkurangan 12 sen kepada RM2.18, Kelington menguncup lima sen kepada RM8.58, dan YTL Power International turun empat sen kepada RM5.64. Di papan indeks, Indeks FBM Mid 70 menambah 28.14 mata kepada 17,510.07, Indeks FBM Emas meningkat 33.81 mata kepada 12,204.38, Indeks FBM Top 100 naik 32.24 mata kepada 11,989.92, Indeks FBM Emas Syariah bertambah 22.28 mata kepada 12,082.60, manakala Indeks FBM ACE meningkat 31.41 mata kepada 5,560.87. Mengikut sektor, Indeks Produk dan Perkhidmatan Perindustrian naik 0.59 mata kepada 179.11, Indeks Tenaga naik 2.57 mata kepada 835.60, Indeks Perkhidmatan Kewangan meningkat 97.59 mata kepada 19,138.10, manakala Indeks Perladangan melonjak 2.23 mata kepada 9,058.78. – Bernama

title: 'CIMB Considers Selling Philippine Business — Bloomberg
body: '(Oct 6): CIMB Group Holdings Bhd (KL:CIMB) is exploring a sale of its business in the Philippines as part of efforts to streamline and focus on bigger markets for growth, according to people with knowledge of the matter. The Malaysian lender is working with a financial adviser on the potential divestment and has reached out to prospective buyers to gauge interest, said the people, asking not to be identified because the process is private. A deal could value the business at as much as US$200 million (RM817 million), the people said. Deliberations are ongoing and CIMB may still decide not to sell, they said. A representative for CIMB didn’t respond to requests for comment. CIMB entered the Philippines in December 2018, and by September 2025 had 10 million customers, according to its website. CIMB also has a presence in Indonesia, Singapore, Thailand, Cambodia and Vietnam, as well as some operations in China, Hong Kong and the UK. The group said in August that its overall net income was RM1.94 billion in the second quarter, and that it’s continuing to “reallocate capital away from underperforming businesses”. CIMB announced in May that it was selling its automotive financing portfolio in Thailand. CIMB’s shares hit a 15-year high in January but have fallen 14% since, giving it a market value of about US$20.4 billion. title: 'A record earnings run
body: 'This article first appeared in The Edge Malaysia Weekly on October 5, 2026 - October 11, 2026 CIMB Group Holdings Bhd Despite an increasingly challenging banking landscape, CIMB Group Holdings Bhd (KL:CIMB) has continued to set new earnings benchmarks, hitting a record net profit in 2024 before surpassing it with a fresh record in 2025. Net profit at the country’s second largest banking group and Asean’s fifth largest by assets rose 1.7% to RM7.86 billion in the financial year ended Dec 31, 2025 (FY2025), from RM7.73 billion a year earlier. That followed a 10.7% increase in FY2024 and a much sharper 28.3% jump in FY2023 to RM6.98 billion. The steady rise in earnings translated into a risk-weighted compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 19.6% over the three years — the highest among its peers. This made CIMB this year’s winner of The Edge Billion Ringgit Club (BRC) award for Highest growth in profit after tax over three years in the financial services sector, among banks that have a market capitalisation of at least RM10 billion. It also won in the BRC Super Big Cap category for companies with a market capitalisation of above RM40 billion. It is the third year running that CIMB has won in both categories, marking how far the group has come since the Covid-19 pandemic. Its return on equity (ROE) improved from 10.7% in 2023 to 11.2% in 2024 and 11.3% in 2025, from just 9% in 2022. Thanks to its strong share price appreciation and attractive dividends, CIMB also clinched this year’s award for highest returns to shareholders over three years in the Super Big Cap category for companies with a market cap of over RM40 billion. CIMB’s shareholder returns grew at a CAGR of 20.2% over the three years — ahead of the competition — as its share price shot up to RM7.55 on March 31, 2026, from RM4.35 on March 31, 2023. The returns reflect the higher dividends that shareholders received as profits grew. CIMB increased its dividend per share from 43 sen in 2023 to 47 sen in 2024, before declaring 47.1 sen for FY2025. Each year’s payout included a special dividend of seven sen per share. The latest payout amounted to a record of about RM5.1 billion. Supporting its share price is the fact that the group has committed to returning up to RM2 billion of additional capital to shareholders by 2027 through special dividends and/or share buybacks, subject to market conditions and regulatory approvals. This year, given a more challenging macroeconomic backdrop, including a prolonged conflict in the Middle East macroeconomics, CIMB’s 1HFY2026 financial performance softened from the previous corresponding period. Net profit for the period fell a marginal 0.2% year on year (y-o-y) to RM3.85 billion, while revenue slid to RM10.97 billion from RM11.10 billion. Be that as it may, it delivered an annualised ROE of 11%, in line with its target of 11% to 11.5% for the full year. It announced an all-cash first interim dividend of 19.65 sen per share, based on a consistent payout ratio of 55.5%, which translated into a total dividend payout of RM2.1 billion. Notably, asset quality remained broadly stable, with its gross impaired loan ratio at an all-time low of 1.6% at end-June, compared with 1.7% three months earlier. Group CEO Novan Amirudin said the execution momentum for Forward30 — the group’s six-year strategic programme that started running from last year — remained firmly on track. “Our destination is clear: to become the top-of-mind Asean bank by 2030. To get there, we must deliver a sustainable ROE of 12% to 13% by 2027 and compete consistently in the top quartile of our regional peers by 2030,” he said in the group’s latest annual report. Nevertheless, headwinds persist, and the group expects funding cost pressures in Indonesia and competition on loan repricing to weigh on its net interest margin (NIM) this year. CIMB’s NIM stood at 2.04% in 2QFY2026, down four basis points from the previous quarter and down 11bps on a y-o-y basis. A notable development this year is that CIMB’s Thai unit, CIMB Thai Bank, was delisted from the Stock Exchange of Thailand on Sept 12, more than 2½ years after a regulatory process triggered by stricter free-float requirements. CIMB Thai remains a core subsidiary and the delisting is not expected to have a material impact on the lender. The Thai unit is profitable, having posted more than a fivefold y-o-y increase in net profit to THB886.3 million in 2QFY2026. As at Aug 28, CIMB’s share price closed at RM7.96, giving the company a market value of RM86.05 billion. Bloomberg data shows 15 “buy” and five “hold” recommendations on the stock, with no “sell” calls. The 12-month average target price was RM8.88. “CIMB has balance sheet flexibility to navigate NIM pressure, and loan loss coverage buffers to weather any asset quality turbulence,” AmInvestment Bank Research said in a Sept 1 report. “The bank has also consistently proved itself as a strong strategy executor and good capital allocator. Besides, we like CIMB’s stance on returning excess capital, with scope for more beyond the planned RM2 billion programme, especially when its dividend payout ratio is about 10 percentage points below larger peers.” Save by subscribing to us for your print and/or digital copy. title: 'Govt dividend receipts up 1.4% to RM39.55b in 2025 on higher BNM, Khazanah payouts — AG’s report
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 5): The federal government received RM39.55 billion in dividends from its investments in 2025, up by 1.4% from RM39.01 billion a year earlier, as higher payouts from Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) and Khazanah Nasional Bhd outweighed lower receipts from other entities. The dividends came from 20 companies and two statutory bodies, compared with 21 companies and two statutory bodies in 2024. The increase was RM535.06 million compared to last year, according to the latest auditor general’s report released on Monday. Petroliam Nasional Bhd (PETRONAS) paid RM32 billion, unchanged from 2024. BNM paid RM5.25 billion, up from RM2.85 billion, an increase of RM2.4 billion or 84.2%. Khazanah's dividend doubled to RM2 billion from RM1 billion. Bank Simpanan Nasional paid RM25 million, down from RM52 million. Dividends from statutory bodies rose 81.8% to RM5.28 billion, while those from companies fell 5.1% to RM34.27 billion. In all, nine companies and one statutory body paid RM7.43 billion, against RM3.98 billion in 2024, an increase of RM3.45 billion or 86.7%. Twelve companies and one statutory body paid less compared to 2024, as three companies paid the same amount in both years. Piramid Pertama Sdn Bhd, which paid RM2.73 billion in 2024, made no payment in 2025. Dividends from Prokhas Sdn Bhd fell to RM5.6 million from RM56.24 million. Three companies, Perbadanan Nasional Bhd, Malaysia Debt Ventures Bhd and Malaysia Digital Economy Corp Sdn Bhd paid dividends in 2025 after paying none in 2024. title: 'Bursa Malaysia Ends Slightly Higher on Bargain-Hunting
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 – Bursa Malaysia staged a slight recovery on Friday, October 2, 2026, as bargain-hunting emerged following a recent sharp sell-off. However, the rebound lacked strong upward momentum as broader Asian markets remained under pressure ahead of crucial United States labour market data releases. At the 5:00 PM close, the benchmark FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) rose marginally by 0.51 points, or 0.03 per cent, to end at 1,630.87 compared to Thursday’s close of 1,630.36. The index, which opened 3.51 points higher at 1,633.87, fluctuated between an intraday low of 1,630.63 and a high of 1,640.78 throughout the session. Overall market breadth turned positive at closing, with gainers outpacing decliners 585 to 541, while 558 counters traded unchanged, 1,089 remained untraded, and 24 were suspended. Total trading volume surged to 4.23 billion units valued at RM2.70 billion, up from 3.10 billion units worth RM2.70 billion recorded on Thursday. Stock Movers and Sector Performance Key heavyweights delivered mixed closing results: - IHH Healthcare: Added 10 sen to RM7.80. - Maybank: Rose 7 sen to RM10.02. - Tenaga Nasional: Firmed 6 sen to RM12.96. - Public Bank: Eased 1 sen to RM4.66. - CIMB: Dropped 4 sen to RM7.65. In active trading, JCY International jumped 10.5 sen to 66 sen, V.S Industry gained 2 sen to 29 sen, and PUC added 1 sen to 4.5 sen. Jaks Resources remained flat at 18 sen, while Zetrix AI declined 5 sen to 11.5 sen. Technology and industrial counters led the top gainers list: - Malaysian Pacific Industries: Surged RM1.28 to RM42.40. - UWC: Rallied 47 sen to RM7.57. - Vitrox: Bounced 46 sen to RM10.46. - United Plantations: Advanced 42 sen to RM31.38. - UMS Integration: Climbed 38 sen to RM9.03. Top decliners were led by Nestle, which dropped 48 sen to RM89.52, and Kuala Lumpur Kepong, down 42 sen to RM21.00. Enra shed 25.5 sen to 72.5 sen, while Allianz Malaysia and Hong Leong Bank fell 20 sen each to RM20.80 and RM22.64, respectively. Across the board: - The FBM Mid 70 Index jumped 122.94 points to 17,481.93. - The FBM Emas Shariah Index climbed 47.31 points to 12,060.32. - The FBM ACE Index improved 46.49 points to 5,529.46. - The FBM Emas Index added 27.04 points to 12,170.57. - The FBM Top 100 Index advanced 24.52 points to 11,957.68. On a sectoral basis, the Plantation Index gained 29.97 points to 9,056.55 and the Industrial Products and Services Index edged up 0.79 points to 178.52. Conversely, the Financial Services Index dropped 20.40 points to 19,040.51, and the Energy Index shed 1.98 points to 833.03. –NMT

Together, we are making it easier for eligible customers to move from purchasing a property to creating a home that meets their lifestyle and investment goals," Vee Loc added. body: 'The local market drifted lower on Wednesday, weighed down by profit- taking among selected index heavyweights, with declines led by the transportation and banking sectors.
