title: 'Bursa Malaysia Retreats After Opening Higher On Selling Pressure
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 7 – Bursa Malaysia opened higher on Wednesday, October 7, 2026, but retreated shortly after as selling pressure in key financial and industrial heavyweights dragged down the benchmark index. At 9:11 AM, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) fell 3.68 points to 1,629.67 compared to Tuesday’s close of 1,633.35. The benchmark index had initially opened 0.19 points higher at 1,633.54. Despite the drop in the main index, market breadth remained positive, with gainers outpacing decliners 221 to 180, while 306 counters were unchanged, 2,083 untraded, and 13 suspended. Total trading volume stood at 327.37 million units valued at RM150.56 million. Heavyweight Pressure and Active Stock Movements Selective profit-taking in banking and industrial counters pulled the composite index down by a combined 7.23 points: - Heavyweight Decliners: Hong Leong Bank slipped 10 sen to RM21.98, CIMB lost 15 sen to RM7.55, and Press Metal Aluminium dropped six sen to RM7.13. Additionally, AMMB fell five sen to RM6.42, Petronas Gas erased eight sen to RM17.20, and Mr D.I.Y. edged down one sen to RM1.24. - Heavyweight Gainers: IHH Healthcare gained three sen to RM7.94, while Maybank rose two sen to RM9.99. - Active Counters: Glovemakers saw buying momentum, with Top Glove advancing 5.5 sen to 93 sen and Supermax adding 2.5 sen to 48.5 sen. Zetrix AI and Ni Hsin both shed half a sen to 8.5 sen and 37 sen, respectively, while Metronic Global traded flat at half a sen. Top Market Movers and Sectoral Performance Technology and industrial stocks featured prominently among the morning’s top gainers and decliners: - Top Gainers: Malaysian Pacific Industries led gains, surging 62 sen to RM45.58, followed by Nestle (up 32 sen to RM91.58), Mi Technovation (up 19 sen to RM6.19), Critical Holdings (up 12 sen to RM2.81), and Hengyuan Refining Company (up nine sen to RM3.55). - Top Decliners: TMK Chemical fell eight sen to RM2.61, Pekat dropped five sen to RM2.91, while Stratus Global and Solarvest each lost four sen to RM3.09 and RM4.33, respectively. Malaysia Smelting declined three sen to RM1.65. On the broader index board, the FBM Mid 70 Index added 61.25 points to 17,795.36, the FBM Emas Shariah Index gained 26.12 points to 12,185.10, and the FBM ACE Index edged up 0.94 points to 5,659.86. Conversely, the FBM Emas Index shed 5.46 points to 12,227.41 and the FBM Top 100 Index dropped 9.15 points to 12,006.63. Across sectors, the Financial Services Index declined 134.06 points to 18,933.94, and the Industrial Products and Services Index dropped 0.09 points to 180.32. On the positive side, the Energy Index climbed 6.79 points to 847.51 and the Plantation Index gained 9.57 points to 9,051.74. –NMT

title: 'Bursa opens marginally higher on easing US Treasury yields, Fed tone
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia rebounded to open marginally higher on Friday, as easing US Treasury yields and a measured tone from the Federal Reserve provided some relief to market sentiment. title: 'PTT Synergy beli 4 kilang dalam pembinaan bernilai RM32 juta di Klang sebelum disewakan
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR 5 Okt — PTT Synergy Group Berhad bakal memperluas portfolio hartanah dengan pemerolehan empat unit kilang bernilai hampir RM32 juta di Klang, Selangor, yang disasarkan menjana pendapatan sewa berulang daripada penyewa industri. Menerusi makluman tambahan kepada Bursa Malaysia, ia berkata anak syarikat tidak langsung milik penuhnya, PTT Assets Sdn Bhd, akan memperoleh empat bidang tanah bersama unit kilang yang sedang atau akan dibina dengan jumlah pertimbangan tunai RM31.997 juta. Menurut kumpulan tersebut, pemerolehan itu bertujuan mengembangkan portfolio pelaburan hartanah kumpulan dan mewujudkan aliran pendapatan sewa berulang menerusi penyewaan keempat-empat unit kilang kepada penyewa industri. "PTT merancang memulakan proses mencari penyewa serta rundingan pajakan sepanjang tempoh pembinaan, dengan operasi sewaan disasarkan bermula selepas projek siap dan milikan kosong diserahkan, tertakluk kepada kerja pengubahsuaian yang diperlukan," katanya. Keempat-empat hartanah dijangka disiapkan dalam tempoh 36 bulan daripada tarikh perjanjian jual beli (SPA) masing-masing, dengan kerja pembinaan telah bermula pada 7 Januari 2026 dan kini mencapai sehingga peringkat rangka struktur bangunan, atau kira-kira 55% siap. Dari segi pembiayaan, risiko pembelian itu disokong kelulusan pinjaman daripada CIMB Bank Berhad dengan margin pembiayaan 90%, selain rebat Bumiputera 10% yang diberikan penjual. Berdasarkan terma pembayaran, 10% daripada harga pembelian perlu dibayar sebaik sahaja setiap SPA ditandatangani, manakala baki bayaran dibuat secara berperingkat mengikut kemajuan pembinaan sehingga notis milikan kosong dikeluarkan. "Pembelian itu turut mengambil kira transaksi hartanah perindustrian berdekatan, termasuk sebuah kilang berkembar di Bukit Raja Prime Industrial Park seluas 1,854.99 meter persegi yang didagangkan pada RM8.5 juta pada Jun 2026," jelas PTT. Satu lagi perbandingan ialah kilang berkembar di Bukit Raja 3 Industrial Park berkeluasan 2,024.99 meter persegi yang direkodkan pada harga RM7.689 juta pada Mac 2026. Sekiranya penjual gagal menyerahkan milikan kosong dalam tempoh 36 bulan daripada tarikh SPA, penjual perlu membayar ganti rugi dipersetujui pada kadar 5% setahun berdasarkan jumlah bayaran yang telah dibuat PTT sehingga tarikh penyerahan sebenar. Dari segi kedudukan kewangan, nisbah penggearan proforma PTT dijangka meningkat kepada 2.01 kali selepas pemerolehan berbanding 1.91 kali setakat 30 Jun 2025, berdasarkan kedudukan kewangan proforma yang dinyatakan syarikat. - DagangNews.com

title: 'Cover Story: How the AI tidal wave is reshaping the jobs market
body: 'This article first appeared in The Edge Malaysia Weekly on September 21, 2026 - September 27, 2026 FOR engineering outfit owner John, using artificial intelligence (AI) in his work has been a game changer. He “trains” the AI to write codes in the company’s style and now merely checks to ensure that the codes are written correctly. “I use AI to write more routine codes and it has helped me cut down coding time significantly, where a few days of work can be accomplished in 20 minutes. But I still need a few employees because engineers need to be at the physical location to make sure hardware is properly installed and conduct test runs,” he says. These days, the use of AI is prevalent in all aspects of life, in various sectors of the economy and professions, and more so among white-collar workers. Early research has shown that AI has, by some measure, improved the productivity of workers, but it still depends on the complexity of tasks and the user’s ability in AI prompting. Even so, AI is increasingly becoming part of everyday life. As a result, companies will soon be able to achieve the same outcomes with fewer workers — or, in some roles, none at all. The concern among white-collar workers about AI displacing jobs is real. Jobstreet’s Workplace Happiness Index found that while only around one-third of Malaysian workers feel “very” or “extremely” concerned about AI affecting their job security, the score is even higher among professional services workers, coming in at 47%. While there is no evidence of massive job loss as a result of AI at this juncture, recruitment agencies observe that job postings for certain roles have been declining. Jobstreet by SEEK in Malaysia managing director Nicholas Lam says AI is certainly putting pressure on some forms of white-collar work, particularly roles involving repetitive, standardised or administrative tasks, many of which are being automated. Current data points, however, more towards roles being redesigned than entire professions being replaced. “The clearest early signs of pressure are in selected content and administrative roles. Job ads for positions such as content writer, copywriter, secretary and graphic designer declined between 2024 and 1H2026. We see these trends as directional indicators that automation may be changing how these roles are structured, rather than proof of one-for-one job replacement,” Lam says. This observation is consistent with a May report by the International Labour Organization (ILO), which found that studies using job postings and online labour-platform data show a significant decline in demand for skills associated with routine writing and translation, following the diffusion of generative AI (GenAI) tools, alongside increased demand for AI-related skills such as machine learning and natural language processing. PwC Malaysia managing partner Soo Hoo Khoon Yean argues that the gradual redesign of work does not necessarily imply that workers will be displaced. Instead, he says, it points to a gradual shift in the mix of capabilities and skills required in those roles. “There may be a growing divide between workers who are able to integrate AI into their workflows and adapt to evolving skill requirements, and those who are unable to,” Soo Hoo says. “As AI becomes more capable, competitive advantage will increasingly come from areas where human strengths like context, judgement and accountability matter most. This includes making high-stakes decisions, solving nuanced problems, managing stakeholder relationships, and bringing together insights from different disciplines to create solutions that AI alone cannot deliver.” Such expectations are starting to show up in the hiring landscape in Malaysia, with AI or digital tools becoming more common in the workplace. Randstad Malaysia associate director, emerging technology recruitment Dylan Long sees a clear shift in Malaysia’s hiring landscape, where employers are increasingly prioritising talent who are adept in AI and digital tools. “This trend is no longer confined to specialised tech departments; instead, having basic knowledge and practical experience with AI has rapidly evolved into a fundamental, baseline requirement for almost any professional role. There is an immense demand for individuals who demonstrate high digital agility,” Long says. He adds that a proactive willingness to embrace self-directed learning and integrate AI into one’s routine work has become a powerful, highly attractive differentiator in the current market. Statistics from Jobstreet confirm this change in the hiring landscape. According to Lam, the recruitment agency’s data shows that 70% of employers factor AI knowledge into hiring decisions, while one in three treat AI capability as a core hiring requirement. At the same time, demand for dedicated AI hiring is also increasing rapidly, notes Lam. AI-labelled job ads grew by 131% year on year in 2025. In 1H2026, the number of AI-labelled job ads was already 24% higher than the total for the whole of 2025, he says. One question that has often been raised is whether junior hiring will be reduced as a result of AI proliferation. A Gartner Inc survey carried out late last year found that 22% of chief human resources officers in the US reported that at least one business leader in their organisation has stopped hiring for entry-level roles as a result of AI automation. Some argue that removing the routine or repetitive tasks traditionally assigned to junior staff — often a training ground for developing judgement and gaining crucial experience — could ultimately hurt organisations by weakening their future talent pipeline. According to Soo Hoo, however, PwC’s global research shows that the bar is now higher for junior talent, with emotional quotient, judgement and leadership skills — qualities normally expected of senior hires — being prioritised. “Organisations will need to rethink how early-career talent is developed, including creating new pathways through which early-career employees can learn through application and experience,” he says. “Traditional apprenticeship models built largely around repetitive tasks may need to evolve into more structured experiences that accelerate the development of these broader capabilities.” Sufficient AI talent in Malaysia? While employers today want workers who can use AI in ways that help create value, there is also a need for AI developer roles in the country, notes Soo Hoo. “Malaysia needs to strengthen both the depth and breadth of its AI talent base. Findings from our 2026 Global AI Jobs Barometer indicate that AI-related roles in Malaysia are currently concentrated in roles that apply AI in business functions (AI user roles) rather than roles focused on developing core AI technologies (AI developer roles),” he says. Soo Hoo cautions that the pipeline of specialised AI talent in Malaysia may not be sustainable for the country’s long-term ambitions, given the pace at which AI is evolving. “Malaysia needs both AI user and AI developer roles in our journey towards realising our AI Nation 2030 aspirations. We need to expand the pool of highly specialised engineers, data scientists and technical experts who can develop and commercialise homegrown digital innovation. At the same time, we must equip workers across sectors with AI literacy, applied skills and judgement to use these technologies productively and responsibly,” he explains. Having said that, every paradigm change will have its drawbacks. Human resources practitioners are reporting that, because of the speed at which the AI world is moving, employees are starting to experience AI fatigue, or “AI brain fry”, as they try to keep pace with the changes. “Companies need to think about the pace at which and direction in which they are adopting AI in their systems and processes. AI fatigue is a real issue and it’s not because employees are not eager to learn. This could result in a decrease, instead of an increase, in efficiency and productivity,” says an HR practitioner. A human resources director with a local company says some employees might not want to go down the AI rabbit hole. “We have reskilling programmes where we reassign certain affected roles to other areas in the company. But some of our employees, typically those who are closer to retirement, say they would rather opt for an early retirement plan, instead of reskilling,” notes the director. State of the labour market Minister of Economic Affairs Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said last Friday that a total of 68,177 workers lost their jobs from January to Sept 16, representing an increase of 15,196 over the same period last year. A recent report on the Social Security Organisation’s Employment Insurance Scheme (EIS) shows that professionals, managers, executives and technicians was the occupation category that saw the highest retrenchment rate, at 51% of the total loss of employment (LOE) benefit applications. It is not a new phenomenon, however, and has been in line with the data from 2021 to 2025. While some have attributed the higher retrenchment numbers partly to the increased adoption of AI or automation in companies, Maybank Investment Bank group chief economist Suhaimi Illias says it is still too early to determine the extent to which AI is driving retrenchments. He points out that Malaysia’s level of AI adoption, compared to other countries around the world, is still moderate. Citing the Microsoft AI Economy Institute’s Global AI Diffusion Scoring, he highlights that Malaysia ranked 51 out of 147 countries, with AI users accounting for 21.8% of the working-age population as at 1Q2026. Countries ranked among the top 20 have AI adoption rates ranging from more than 30% to 70%. “There are also other factors behind the higher share of skilled-worker retrenchments. Voluntary/Mutual Separation Schemes or Early Retirement Planning (VSS/MSS/ERP) have consistently ranked among the top three reasons for retrenchments and were the leading reason between 2023 and 2025. Higher-skilled employees may be more inclined to participate in such schemes, given attractive payouts,” Suhaimi says. He adds that the spike in total retrenchments may also reflect companies managing rising cost pressures through headcount reductions. This year, while the Consumer Price Index has remained moderate at 1.9% y-o-y in June, from 1.4% in February, the Producer Price Index has seen a spike to 9.2% y-o-y, from -3.4%, implying that companies have not passed down much of their higher cost to consumers so far. Interestingly, the country’s unemployment rate has held steady around 3% despite rising retrenchments. Suhaimi explains that because job placements continue to outpace layoffs, the economy is still net-positive for job creation. In 1H2026, placements reached 74,874, significantly higher than the 47,030 retrenchments. The way forward for employees With 620,000 jobs in Malaysia expected to be reshaped by AI, digitalisation and the green economy over the next three to five years, Jobstreet’s Lam warns that early-career professionals must learn to use these technologies both practically and responsibly. “AI literacy should increasingly be treated as a baseline capability,” he adds. Still, being literate in digital tools alone is not enough. Randstad’s Long points out the younger generation are naturally adept at using and eager to adopt new technology, but global employers still prefer “job-ready” candidates who have practical experience. “New graduates can prepare by actively seeking out structured internships, graduate trainee programmes, and on-the-job training opportunities that offer direct exposure to complex, real-world projects,” he says. “In fact, according to the Randstad 2026 Job Market Outlook and Salary Guide report, continuous learning has become such a non-negotiable for long-term career security that 56% of Gen Z talent in Malaysia would outright reject a job offer if it did not provide clear learning and development pathways to future-proof their skills.” Meanwhile, Long notes that mid- to late-career professionals must future-proof themselves by blending their vast experience with modern technological efficiency. Ultimately, Lam concludes, today’s workforce — regardless of seniority — should strive to work with AI while sharpening the human and commercial skills that technology cannot easily replicate. A recent report on the Social Security Organisation’s Employment Insurance Scheme (EIS) shows that professionals, managers, executives and technicians was the occupation category that saw the highest retrenchment rate, at 51% of the total loss of employment (LOE) benefit applications. It is not a new phenomenon, however, and has been in line with the data from 2021 to 2025. While some have attributed the higher retrenchment numbers partly to the increased adoption of AI or automation in companies, Maybank Investment Bank group chief economist Suhaimi Illias says it is still too early to determine the extent to which AI is driving retrenchments. He points out that Malaysia’s level of AI adoption, compared to other countries around the world, is still moderate. Citing the Microsoft AI Economy Institute’s Global AI Diffusion Scoring, he highlights that Malaysia ranked 51 out of 147 countries, with AI users accounting for 21.8% of the working-age population as at 1Q2026. Countries ranked among the top 20 have AI adoption rates ranging from more than 30% to 70%. “There are also other factors behind the higher share of skilled-worker retrenchments. Voluntary/Mutual Separation Schemes or Early Retirement Planning (VSS/MSS/ERP) have consistently ranked among the top three reasons for retrenchments and were the leading reason between 2023 and 2025. Higher-skilled employees may be more inclined to participate in such schemes, given attractive payouts,” Suhaimi says. He adds that the spike in total retrenchments may also reflect companies managing rising cost pressures through headcount reductions. This year, while the Consumer Price Index has remained moderate at 1.9% y-o-y in June, from 1.4% in February, the Producer Price Index has seen a spike to 9.2% y-o-y, from -3.4%, implying that companies have not passed down much of their higher cost to consumers so far. Interestingly, the country’s unemployment rate has held steady around 3% despite rising retrenchments. Suhaimi explains that because job placements continue to outpace layoffs, the economy is still net-positive for job creation. In 1H2026, placements reached 74,874, significantly higher than the 47,030 retrenchments. The way forward for employees With 620,000 jobs in Malaysia expected to be reshaped by AI, digitalisation and the green economy over the next three to five years, Jobstreet’s Lam warns that early-career professionals must learn to use these technologies both practically and responsibly. “AI literacy should increasingly be treated as a baseline capability,” he adds. Still, being literate in digital tools alone is not enough. Randstad’s Long points out the younger generation are naturally adept at using and eager to adopt new technology, but global employers still prefer “job-ready” candidates who have practical experience. “New graduates can prepare by actively seeking out structured internships, graduate trainee programmes, and on-the-job training opportunities that offer direct exposure to complex, real-world projects,” he says. “In fact, according to the Randstad 2026 Job Market Outlook and Salary Guide report, continuous learning has become such a non-negotiable for long-term career security that 56% of Gen Z talent in Malaysia would outright reject a job offer if it did not provide clear learning and development pathways to future-proof their skills.” Meanwhile, Long notes that mid- to late-career professionals must future-proof themselves by blending their vast experience with modern technological efficiency. Ultimately, Lam concludes, today’s workforce — regardless of seniority — should strive to work with AI while sharpening the human and commercial skills that technology cannot easily replicate. title: 'Four Sikh scholars show the opportunities beyond SPM
body: 'By Manjit Singh | Malaysia | Four Malaysian Sikh students have secured fully funded scholarships for overseas studies in 2026, showing how strong academic results, co-curricular involvement and persistence can open doors to leading universities abroad. Dilpreet Kaur, Gurmansimran Kaur, Priety Kaur and Satishver Singh all began their scholarship journeys after completing the Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM), the national public examination taken by all Form 5 secondary school students in Malaysia at the end of their 11th year of formal education. Their scholarships supported their progression through pre-university studies and on to undergraduate programmes overseas. SEE ALSO: Malaysian Sikh Education Aid Fund (MSEAF) Dilpreet will pursue a BSc in Chemistry at Imperial College London, while Gurmansimran will study Accounting and Finance at the University of Manchester. Priety will pursue an MEng in Electrical and Electronic Engineering, also at Manchester, while Satishver is pursuing Data Science at the University of California, Berkeley. Beyond their academic achievements, the four say scholarship applicants should start preparing early and recognise that selectors often look beyond examination grades. Leadership roles, competitions, volunteering, research, internships, community activities and other experiences can help students develop the skills and interests that strengthen an application. Their other key advice: apply widely. Scholarship applications can involve setbacks and rejection, they say, but students should continue looking for opportunities instead of allowing one unsuccessful application to end the journey. They also encourage students to seek internships or research experience connected with their intended university courses. Such exposure can help applicants better understand their chosen fields while demonstrating genuine interest beyond the classroom. Maintaining balance is equally important. The scholars say academic ambition need not come at the expense of friendships, community involvement or personal wellbeing. Co-curricular activities can build confidence, social skills and networks while helping students discover interests they may eventually pursue professionally. WHAT DO THEY SAY Dilpreet’s message to other students is simple: “You are more capable than you think. Believe in yourself.” Gurmansimran stresses the lasting value of education, while Priety encourages students moving away from home to remain independent but grounded and positive. Satishver advises youngsters not to allow setbacks to define their journey: “It is never too late to turn the page, rewrite the plot or begin a new chapter.” Collectively, the four encourage students to look seriously at scholarship opportunities after SPM. Major scholarship programmes available to Malaysian students include those offered by JPA, PETRONAS, Bank Negara Malaysia, Yayasan Khazanah, Yayasan Tenaga Nasional, Yayasan Telekom Malaysia, Yayasan Sime Darby, Shell Malaysia, Yayasan UEM, CIMB ASEAN and Yayasan Gamuda. Application periods, eligibility requirements and funding terms vary, so students should regularly check the respective organisations’ official scholarship pages. Their common message to younger students is to aim high, ask questions, seek opportunities and apply — even when a scholarship appears highly competitive. “We hope to see more Sikh students pursuing their ambitions on a global stage,” they said. title: 'High Court to rule Oct 23 on Maritime Network’s bid to keep RHB accounts open
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: The High Court here today fixed Oct 23 to rule on a shipping company’s bid to restrain RHB Bank Berhad from closing two of its long-standing accounts, pending the disposal of its full suit.   Judicial Commissioner Elesabet Paya Wan set the date after hearing submissions from P. Taneswaran, acting for Maritime Network Sdn Bhd, and the bank’s counsel, Gan Khong Aik.   Taneswaran submitted that the bank had failed to establish any breach of terms or requirements by the plaintiff, Maritime Network, that would justify closing its accounts.

title: 'Kuala Lumpur News
body:
'

JETOUR Launches T2 i-DM Hybrid

JETOUR Malaysia has launched the T2 i-DM, a plug-in hybrid SUV priced at RM162,800.
It pairs a 1.5-litre turbocharged petrol engine with a dual-motor electric system for a combined output of up to 265kW and 610Nm. JETOUR claims up to 1,200km of combined driving range and more than 100km on electric power alone. The battery is an 18.4kWh lithium iron phosphate unit, and DC fast charging takes it from 30% to 80% in 27 minutes or less, according to the company.
The first 2,000 customers get an Early Bird Package worth up to RM3,000, with a choice of a free 7kW wallbox charger with installation or RM2,000 in ChargeSini charging credit, plus a free V2L adapter cable. Financing rates start at 1.68%, subject to terms and conditions.
The car comes with a seven-year or 150,000km vehicle warranty, an eight-year or 160,000km battery warranty and five free services.

New Jalan Alor Seafood Restaurant

Canteen Malaya has opened on Jalan Alor in Kuala Lumpur, offering live seafood and an open kitchen in an air-conditioned, four-level restaurant.
Diners choose their own crab, tiger prawns or fish, which is then cooked to order in view of the dining floor. Crab is the focus of the menu, with more than 30 flavours and preparations, including 12 signature dishes such as Salted Egg Crab, Kam Heong Crab and White Pepper Crab.
The restaurant seats up to 700 guests. The ground and first floors hold the dining areas and private rooms, and the second floor has an event hall for up to 250.
“Our focus is simple: to serve fresh, honest seafood to everyday diners,” said Ms Patricia Wong, Management Representative of Canteen Malaya. “We wanted an open kitchen where guests can watch their seafood being prepared, in a space where they can take their time over a meal.”
Canteen Malaya is at 28, 28A-C, 30 and 30A-C Jalan Alor and is open daily from 11am to 2am.

L&G AGM Backs Growth Push

Land & General Berhad (L&G) secured shareholder approval for all nine resolutions at its 63rd AGM today, including a final dividend of 0.8 sen per share for FY2026. Combined with the 0.2 sen interim dividend paid in May, total FY2026 dividends reached 1.0 sen — up 25% from FY2025. The final dividend is payable 16 October to shareholders on record as at 2 October.
Shareholders also approved the re-election of three directors, the reappointment of KPMG PLT as auditors, a general share issuance mandate, and a proposed share buy-back.
The vote follows a record FY2026: Group revenue rose 70.6% to RM490.5 million, pre-tax profit climbed 25.6% to RM74.2 million, and net profit attributable to owners grew 38.7% to RM50.5 million. The momentum carried into 1QFY2027, with revenue up 61.5% year-on-year to RM159.0 million and net profit up 88.7% to RM21.5 million. Unbilled sales stood at RM513 million as at 30 June, backed by RM1.5 billion in planned FY2027 launches.
L&G is also broadening beyond its traditional property development base into a three-pillar structure spanning property, education (via its Sri Bestari schools) and industrial development. The centrepiece is a planned industrial park on its roughly 2,500-acre Lembah Beringin landbank, with the first phase targeted for FY2027 and revenue recognition expected from FY2028, alongside a RM500 million stratified industrial and commercial project on 13.74 acres in Tampoi, Johor.

KEB Inks IPO Underwriting Deal

Property developer KEB Berhad has signed an underwriting agreement with M & A Securities Sdn Bhd ahead of its planned listing on the ACE Market of Bursa Malaysia.
M & A Securities will underwrite 66.18 million new shares, comprising 44.12 million shares for the Malaysian public and 22.06 million shares for eligible directors, employees and contributors to the Group.
The IPO involves a public issue of 138.54 million new shares and an offer for sale of 88.24 million existing shares, totalling 226.78 million shares. The remaining shares will be placed privately with MITI-approved Bumiputera investors and selected investors.
Proceeds from the public issue will go towards landbank acquisition, project working capital, repayment of bank borrowings and listing expenses.
Founded in 2004, KEB has completed 14 projects and has two ongoing developments worth RM773.29 million in gross development value (GDV), with four future projects valued at RM940.74 million. Its construction arm, KEB Utama Sdn Bhd, is a CIDB Grade G7 contractor.
M & A Securities is the principal adviser, sponsor, placement agent and underwriter, while Eco Asia Capital Advisory Sdn Bhd is the financial adviser.

CARSOME Academy Marks Fifth Year

CARSOME Academy has marked its fifth anniversary with more than RM2 million in funding and scholarships to train Malaysians for automotive careers.
This includes the RM1.65 million Accelerate with TVET Programme, anchored by Maybank Islamic Berhad, and more than RM350,000 in Selangor State Government scholarships for Asnaf and B40 students.
The Academy has also signed an MoU with JETOUR Automobile Malaysia to offer work placements, and launched two automotive sales TVET programmes with SKM certification.
Since 2021, 593 students have registered with the Academy, with 90% finding jobs within three months.

Aneka Jaringan Wins RM26.2m Contract

Basement and foundation specialist Aneka Jaringan Holdings Berhad has secured a RM26.20 million contract for a high-rise serviced apartment project in Kuala Lumpur.
Its wholly-owned subsidiary, Aneka Jaringan Sdn Bhd, accepted the Letter of Award from WDA Architects Sdn Bhd on behalf of Exsim YKS 54 Sdn Bhd. The job covers earthworks, piling and pile caps, retaining wall and substructure works for a 53-storey, 394-unit serviced apartment development on Jalan Yap Kwan Seng.
The contract began on 15 September 2026 and is due for completion by 14 August 2028. The Group said it is expected to contribute positively to earnings and net assets for the financial years ending 31 August 2027 and 2028.

DC Healthcare Opens Four Clinics

Medical aesthetic services provider DC Healthcare Holdings Berhad has opened four new clinics across Johor, Selangor and Penang between July and September 2026.
Three are under its Dr Chong Clinic brand, in Muar, USJ Taipan and Setia Alam, while the Penang Greenlane outlet marks the launch of a new brand, DC Plus Clinic.
The expansion comes as the Group’s core aesthetic services segment grows, with revenue rising 15% year-on-year to RM20.44 million in Q2 FY2026, and 20% to RM39.12 million for the first half.

EcoSys Launches IPO Prospectus

Industrial solutions provider EcoSys (Malaysia) Berhad has launched its prospectus for an initial public offering on the ACE Market of Bursa Malaysia, aiming to raise RM39.34 million.
The IPO involves a public issue of 145.70 million new shares at RM0.27 each, representing about 25.5% of the company’s enlarged share capital of 571.35 million shares. There is no offer for sale.
EcoSys serves the pan-semiconductor industry through ultra-high purity fabrication of precision engineering components and the development and maintenance of abatement systems.
Most of the proceeds, RM17 million, will go towards expanding its abatement segment, with RM8 million for repaying bank borrowings and RM4.93 million for new machinery and staff. A further RM1.54 million will fund a sales and service centre in India, which accounted for RM38.22 million, or 35.1%, of the Group’s revenue in FYE2025.
M & A Securities Sdn Bhd is the Principal Adviser, Sponsor, Underwriter and Placement Agent, while Eco Asia Capital Advisory Sdn Bhd is the Financial Adviser.

title: 'Bursa Malaysia Closes Lower Amid Cautious Wall Street Influence
body: 'Kuala Lumpur:Bursa Malaysia ended the trading session lower on Thursday due to persistent selling pressure, influenced by a mixed and cautious performance on Wall Street overnight. According to BERNAMA News Agency, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) dropped 20.81 points, or 1.26 percent, closing at 1,630.36, down from the previous day's close of 1,651.17. The index opened slightly weaker at 1,649.87 and fluctuated between 1,630.10 and 1,649.87 throughout the day. The market trend showed a negative breadth, with 750 decliners outpacing 342 gainers, while 495 counters remained unchanged, 1,186 were untraded, and 12 were suspended. Turnover decreased to 3.1 billion units valued at RM2.7 billion, compared to 3.63 billion units worth RM3.62 billion on Wednesday. Mohd Sedek Jantan, the director of investment strategy and country economist at IPPFA Sdn Bhd, noted that the sentiment was cautious, exacerbated by weaker domestic manufacturing activity and continued foreign selling. He highlighted that softer manufacturing momentum and global portfolio rotation exerted pressure on the benchmark index, despite domestic institutional demand providing some balance against foreign outflows. The S and P Global Malaysia Manufacturing Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) slightly dipped below the neutral 50.0 mark, reaching 49.9 in September from 50.2 in August. This marks the first decline in four months following a period of improvement. Regionally, the S and P Global ASEAN Manufacturing PMI decreased to 52.1 in September from 52.3 in August. In terms of specific stocks, Maybank fell four sen to RM9.95, Public Bank lost three sen to RM4.67, and CIMB dropped 10 sen to RM7.69. Tenaga Nasional declined six sen to RM12.90, while IHH Healthcare erased 13 sen to RM7.70. title: 'Bursa Malaysia opens higher on positive Wall Street momentum
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia opened higher on Tuesday, in sync with Wall Street's positive overnight momentum, as muted oil prices following a recovery in West Asia crude exports offset a continued sell-off in US Treasuries. At 9.21am, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) rose 7.14 points, or 0.44 per cent, to 1,638.89 from Monday's close of 1,631.75. The index opened 4.63 points higher at 1,636.38. On the broader market, gainers outpaced losers 272 to 202, with 364 counters unchanged, 1,944 untraded and 13 suspended. Turnover stood at 440.19 million shares worth RM164.76 million. Malacca Securities Sdn Bhd said Wall Street's positive overnight performance saw the Dow Jones Industrial Average, S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite advance by 0.2 per cent, 0.7 per cent and 1.1 per cent, respectively, while the Brent crude oil and 10-year Treasury yield reached US$100.3 per barrel and 5.3 per cent, respectively. "Locally, we expect investors to remain selective ahead of the Budget 2027 announcement, with attention centred on potential beneficiary sectors. "Mechanical and electrical players could continue to see buying interest, supported by the government's emphasis on artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure and Tenaga Nasional Bhd's 500-kilovolt National Grid Backbone project, favouring companies such as MN Holdings Bhd, Southern Cable Group Bhd, and Powerwell Holdings Bhd," it said in a research note today. In addition, Malacca Securities said efforts to reduce non-revenue water could also remain in focus, potentially benefiting companies such as ISF Group Bhd and Ranhill Utilities Bhd. "Lastly, 99 Speed Mart Retail could see renewed buying interest on expectations of higher consumer assistance allocations under Sumbangan Asas Rahmah and Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah," it said. Meanwhile, Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd vice-president of equity research Thong Pak Leng said Wall Street closed firmer, with the Nasdaq notching a fresh record high as traders decided to look past prevailing headwinds and instead focus on AI-related stocks to negate the impacts from escalating bond yields. "For today, we expect the index to hover within the range of 1,630-1,640 as the local bourse may be ripe for some bargain hunting activity," he told Bernama. Among the heavyweights, Maybank and Tenaga Nasional perked up four sen each to RM10.04 and RM13.04, CIMB put on three sen to RM7.76, IHH Healthcare increased two sen to RM7.78, while Public Bank was flat at RM4.71. In active trade, Zetrix AI inched up half a sen to seven sen, Divfex rose one sen to 16.5 sen, Ramssol gained 2.5 sen to 86 sen, while ACE market debutant SLGC eased 3.5 sen to 24.5 sen, and Dagang NeXchange inched down half a sen to 50 sen. Among the top gainers, Batu Kawan expanded RM1.24 sen to RM20.22, Nestle and Kuala Lumpur Kepong gained 20 sen each to RM90.20 and RM21.06, Petronas Dagangan perked up 18 sen to RM19.38, and Genting Plantations strengthened 16 sen to RM5.82. HeiTech Padu led the decliners, falling seven sen to 88 sen, Thong Guan Industries, Sunway Construction Group, and Allianz Malaysia slipped six sen each to RM1.44, RM7.55 and RM20.74, and UMS Integration shrank four sen to RM9.36. On the index board, the FBM Mid 70 Index gained 41.29 points to 17,584.78, the FBM Emas Index appreciated 44.30 points to 12,234.65, the FBM Top 100 Index widened 46.09 points to 12,019.47, the FBM Emas Shariah Index advanced 39.24 points to 12,108.25, and the FBM ACE Index improved 7.73 points to 5,614.34. Sector-wise, the Industrial Products and Services Index inched up 0.16 of a point to 179.13, the Energy Index gained 1.78 points to 831.72, the Financial Services Index jumped 56.47 points to 19,196.61, and the Plantation Index gained 73.78 points to 9,004.81.

title: 'Sunway Construction could bag RM1b mixed-use development contracts near Bukit Chagar — Maybank IB
body:
'

KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 10): Sunway Construction Group Bhd (KL:SUNCON) could win an estimated RM1 billion in podium and tower contracts for an integrated mixed-use development at the Bukit Chagar RTS Link, Johor Bahru, according to Maybank Investment Bank.

The research house noted that the potential win came from a joint venture development between its parent company, Sunway Bhd (KL:SUNWAY), and Mass Rapid Transit Corporation (MRT Corp), which could increase Sunway Construction’s overall net profit by about RM60 million.

Consequently, Maybank IB mantained its “buy” call and RM9.62 target price, pegged to 17.7 times the financial year ending Dec 31, 2027 (FY2027) estimated price earnings.

Previously, Sunway Construction had secured a RM1.5 billion contract to undertake construction works for the rapid transit system (RTS) transit-oriented development at Bukit Chagar, Johor, in a related-party transaction last year.

At the time of writing, Sunway Construction shares were down three sen or 0.38% at RM7.95, valuing the company at RM10.6 billion.

RM11 billion worth of development value surrounding Bukit Chagar station

Analysts estimate that the total development value surrounding the Bukit Chagar station will reach a combined RM11 billion across the three largest surrounding projects.

The commercial opening of the RTS Link in late 2026 or early 2027 is widely anticipated to catalyse property demand and accelerate construction timelines in the zone.

The three anchor projects driving the node represent a combined gross development value of RM11.1 billion, consisting of the RM5 billion Coronation Square, the RM3.5 billion Causewayz Square, and the RM2.6 billion Sunway-MRT Corp integrated development.

Of the trio, Coronation Square — an eight-tower integrated hub comprising offices, residential units, medical facilities, and an Ascott hotel — is slated for completion by 2029.

Meanwhile, the wider Sunway-MRT Corp integrated development will be phased over eight years, with its primary components targeted for completion between 2033 and 2036.

Binastra emerges as major Causewayz Square’s beneficiary

Causewayz Square, a high-density mixed residential and retail project developed by EXSIM Group, is targeted for full completion by December 2030.

Maybank IB highlighted the project's significance for Binastra Corporation Bhd (KL:BNASTRA), noting that the RM1.3 billion worth of contracts secured from this development accounts for approximately 20% of the builder's outstanding order book.

Within this package, the main RM1.2 billion construction job is projected to contribute roughly RM90 million to the group's net profit.

At the time of writing, Binastra Corporation shares were down one sen or 0.4% at RM2.47, valuing the company at RM2.7 billion.

The proposed 50km elevated transit network will comprise 32 stations across the Skudai, Tebrau and Iskandar Puteri corridors, converging at the Bukit Chagar station.

It will serve as the RTS Link’s feeder and last-mile connection, dispersing up to 10,000 cross-border passengers per hour into the Johor Bahru area.

title: 'Daily Brief - 24 Sep 2026
body: 'The local market drifted lower on Wednesday, weighed down by profit-taking among selected index heavyweights, with declines led by the transportation and banking sectors. The FBM KLCI shed 7.07 points to end at 1,676.43, off an early high of 1,685.37 and low of 1,675.15, as losers narrowly beat gainers 549 to 519, on lower turnover of 3.2bn shares worth RM2.99bn. The local benchmark index is expected to remain rangebound as investors await clearer policy signals from the ongoing U.S.-China talks, while the lack of meaningful domestic catalysts is likely to keep market direction subdued. Immediate resistance for the index remains at the June 2026 high (1,722), followed by tougher upside hurdles at the 123.6%FP (1,759) and 138.2%FP (1,805) ahead. Meanwhile, immediate support is maintained at the June 2026 low (1,655), with stronger support coming from the 76.4%FR (1,610) and 61.8%FR (1,564). CIMB need to reinforce support above the 61.8%FR (RM7.43) to enhance recovery potential to the 27/01/26 peak (RM8.50), with next upside hurdles at the 123.6%FP (RM9.17) and 138.2%FP (RM9.58) ahead, while stronger retracement support is found at the 50%FR (RM7.10). Meantime, RHB Bank is attractive to bargain for oversold rebound towards the 50- day ma (RM8.28), with a convincing breakout above the 10/08/26 high (RM8.77) to target the 123.6%FP (RM9.14). Crucial support comes from the 61.8%FR (RM7.36) and 50%FR (RM7.02). Asian markets traded mixed on Wednesday, as regional sentiment remained subdued while investors monitored ongoing geopolitical developments ahead of key U.S.-China talks. Oil prices extended their decline as traders weighed comments from President Donald Trump saying that U.S. officials had a “very good” meeting with an Iranian delegation on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly, although he also threatened to “annihilate” the country if a deal was not reached. Investors also awaited further direction from the upcoming meeting between President Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping, with market participants watching for a possible extension of the trade truce and potential cooperation on AI between the two countries. Nevertheless, AI-linked stocks in the region extended their winning streak underpinned by renewed optimism over chip demand, amid strong consumer take up of Meta's new AI agent. Australia’s S&P/ASX 200 edged higher 0.09% to 8,765.30, while South Korea’s Kospi gained 0.90% to 7,080.92. In the mainland, the Shanghai Composite Index fell 0.39% to 3,936.52, while Hong Kong’s Hang Seng Index slumped 1.01% to 24,834.12. Markets in Japan were closed for a public holiday. Wall Street’s major indexes ended lower overnight as a spike in Treasury yields revived inflation concerns, while investors tracked U.S. diplomatic developments involving Iran and China. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 0.68% to 51,511.59. The S&P 500 slipped 0.75% to 7,706.03, while the Nasdaq Composite dropped 1.13% to 26,936.03. The 10-year Treasury yield surged past 5.11%, reaching its highest level since 2007, as rising oil prices and stronger- than-expected U.S. business activity fueled inflation concerns. Oil prices also moved higher following Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian’s address to the UN, a day after U.S. President Donald Trump warned that he could “annihilate” Iran. The shift in market expectations raised the likelihood of another Federal Reserve rate hike this year, following comments from Governor Michael Barr that “further policy adjustments” would be necessary to push inflation lower. Separately, President Trump is expected to receive Chinese President Xi Jinping at Joint Base Andrews, marking Xi’s first visit to Washington, D.C., in more than a decade. The leaders are expected to discuss extending last year’s trade truce, along with AI regulation and U.S. weapons sales to Taiwan. title: 'HLB Meezani Account-i Offers Cash, Gold, And Cars In New Prize Draws
body: 'HLB Meezani Account-i holders stand a chance to win cash, gold bars, holiday packages, a Proton e.MAS 5, and a Porsche Cayenne in HLB Islamic’s second year of prize draws, which runs from 30 July 2026 to 29 July 2027. There are daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly, and yearly draws, with minimum balances ranging from RM100 to RM60,000 depending on the prize. HLB Islamic announced this year’s prizes at a rewards ceremony in Kuala Lumpur on 29 September 2026, held to mark the account’s first year. The bank said 43% of those who opened the account in its first year were new HLB Islamic customers. The Minimum Balance For Each Prize Each prize has its own minimum balance, and you get one entry for every full multiple of that amount. For example, keeping RM1,000 in the account when the day ends gives 10 entries in the daily draw, since the minimum balance is RM100. For the weekly draw, you get one entry for every RM200. Keeping RM2,500 at the end of the week gives 12 entries, and the extra RM100 doesn’t count. For quarterly and yearly prizes, entries are counted from each month-end balance and added up until the draw. Keeping RM2,000 in the account at the end of each month for a three-month quarter, for example, gives three entries for the 10g gold bar draw. Since the monthly, quarterly, and yearly draws all use your month-end balance, withdrawing money on the last day of the month can reduce your entries for that month, even if you put the money back a few days later. Some Payments And Deposits Can Earn Extra Entries The monthly and quarterly prizes also offer extra entries if you’ve already met the minimum balance for the relevant prize. You can earn additional entries by making at least 10 eligible QR or online payments from the account in a month, or by depositing at least RM2,000 in a single transaction. Doing both in the same month earns one more combo entry. Making 10 payments earns extra entries for the RM500 cash and Touch ‘n Go prizes. A deposit of RM2,000 or more earns extra entries for every prize in the table except the Proton e.MAS 5, which only gets the combo entry when you do both in the same month. The daily, weekly, and yearly draws don’t offer extra entries. Win Limits And Claiming Your Prize You can win the daily prize once a week at most, and the weekly prize once every two weeks. If your name is selected for more than one monthly prize in the same month, you’ll only receive the highest-value prize. The same applies to the quarterly and yearly draws. To qualify for the draws, you need to actively use HLB Connect from the start of each draw period until any prize is handed over. Winners are selected within 30 working days after each draw period ends and notified through the HLB Connect app within 14 working days after that. You have 30 working days from the announcement to claim your prize, after which the bank may award it to another winner. Cash prizes are credited directly into the winner’s HLB Meezani Account-i. Winners are responsible for any taxes or fees related to their prizes, and HLB Islamic may publish winners’ names with part of their IC numbers concealed. Non-cash prizes are handed over within 90 working days. Winners will need their winning letter and IC to collect them. Prizes can’t be exchanged for cash or transferred to someone else. Opening An HLB Meezani Account-i The account is Shariah-compliant and open to individuals who live in Malaysia. You need RM100 to open it and RM50 to keep it open. The account currently has an indicative profit rate of 0.05% p.a., calculated daily and paid monthly, as of 30 September 2026. You can deposit or withdraw money through HLB Islamic branches, ATMs, cash deposit machines, and online channels. Because it’s an investment account rather than a savings account or fixed deposit, HLB Islamic states that the money and returns aren’t guaranteed and the account isn’t protected by Perbadanan Insurans Deposit Malaysia (PIDM). The prize draws come on top of the account’s profit rate, so look at both when deciding where to keep your money. You can also compare the latest savings account and fixed deposit rates on RinggitPlus. You can open the account at an HLB Islamic branch or book an appointment through the HLB Islamic website. The full rules are set out in the campaign’s terms and conditions [PDF]. Follow us on our official WhatsApp channel for the latest money tips and updates.

IMF: Cost-of-living crises have lasting impact on inflation expectations, poverty, IMF says 5.33% on Monday Sharp spikes in food and energy prices will likely become more common, the International Monetary Fund said, warning such crises drive inflation expectations higher for longer, worsen poverty and threaten economic stability. IMF research released on Tuesday examined three decades of strategies used by governments to mitigate price surges, as well as a new economic model that accounts for the higher inflation experienced by poorer households, which spend a higher share of their budgets on daily necessities. (Reuters) US: Oil Rises as Mideast Risks Remain 5.33% on Monday Crude oil climbed toward $90 per barrel on Wednesday, recovering from five-week lows as persistent risks to Middle East energy flows overshadowed signs of rising supply from the region. Iran has intensified attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz in recent days, with the UK Maritime Trade Operations reporting nine incidents so far this month. (Trading Economics) US: Trade deficit widens in August amid strong imports 5.33% on Monday The US trade deficit widened more than expected in August, driven by a surge in imports of goods amid robust domestic demand, keeping trade on track to again subtract from economic growth in the third quarter. The trade shortfall increased 13.7% to US$105.6 billion (RM431.5 billion), the Commerce Department's Bureau of Economic Analysis and Census Bureau said on Tuesday. (Trading Economics) US: 10-Year Treasury Yield Softens from 24-Year High The yield on the 10-year US Treasury note was at 5.26% on Tuesday, pausing a surge that peaked at a 24-year high of 5.33% touched yesterday, tracking the momentary dip in wholesale fuel prices. Oil bids were tamed by signs that some laden tankers passed through the Strait of Hormuz. The 10-year yield has surged over 110bps this year as risks of higher rates from the Federal Reserve, soaring federal deficit spending, and increasing corporate debt supply triggered a plunge in demand for duration. It is the second-highest reading in four years, behind only June’s reading of 71.1. A faster increase was seen for Inventory Levels (58.9 vs 52.8) and Inventory Costs (79.9 vs 78.6) which is also having a significant effect on the warehousing market. Warehousing Capacity shrank the most since March 2022 (39.3 vs 53.5), potentially due to the fact that firms, particularly retailers, had run inventory down a bit and are not rushing goods in now ahead of potential holiday sales. (Trading Economics) US: Gold edges up as dollar, Treasury yields slip Gold ticked up on Tuesday, supported by a pause in the US Treasury yield's rally and a weaker dollar, while investors awaited the minutes of the US Federal Reserve's (Fed) September meeting for fresh clues on its monetary policy outlook. The remarks come ahead of the central bank's two-day policy meeting ending on Oct 30, where new quarterly growth and inflation forecasts will be closely watched for clues on the timing of the next rate hike. (Reuters) JP: 10-year bond sale draws solid demand as yields top 3% Japan’s 10-year government bond auction Tuesday saw stronger demand than the 12-month average as elevated yields underpinned buying. The bid-to-cover ratio was 3.76 compared with 3.29 at the previous sale and a 12-month average of 3.21. Bond futures pared their losses after the result. The benchmark 10-year yield hit 3.115% on Tuesday, matching its highest level since 1996. A sale of the same tenor last month passed smoothly after yields reached 3%. (Bloomberg) JP: Nominal Wage Growth Tops 3% for 7th Month Average cash earnings in Japan increased by 3.8% year-on-year in August 2026, slightly exceeding market expectations for a 3.7% gain and staying above 3% for a seventh month, the longest such run since 1992. While it slowed from a revised 4.3% rise in July, it also marked the 56th consecutive month of nominal wage growth. Regular pay, including base salaries, rose 3.8% to mark continued solid wage growth, while overtime pay accelerated to 5.2% from a revised 4.5% increase in July. (Trading Economics) MY: BNM: Banks working towards fraud alert before transaction is completed Malaysian banks are working towards introducing fraud alert capabilities that can flag potential risks before a transaction is completed. A pilot test involving selected banks is targeted for the first half of 2027 ahead of wider implementation, Bank Negara Malaysia governor Datuk Seri Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour said in his speech text for a conference on financial crime and counter terrorism financing on Tuesday. (The Edge) MY: And France to sign energy transition MOU soon, says Fadillah Malaysia and France are expected to sign a memorandum of understanding (MOU) on energy transition soon to accelerate efforts towards a cleaner and more sustainable future, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof said on Tuesday. Fadillah, who is also the energy transition and water transformation minister, said the matter was discussed during a courtesy call by French Ambassador to Malaysia Marc Abensour at the Parliament building on Tuesday. (Bernama) CIMB: Considers selling Philippine business - Bloomberg CIMB Group Holdings Bhd is exploring a sale of its business in the Philippines as part of efforts to streamline and focus on bigger markets for growth, according to people with knowledge of the matter. The Malaysian lender is working with a financial adviser on the potential divestment and has reached out to prospective buyers to gauge interest, said the people, asking not to be identified because the process is private. It said this in a bourse filing on Tuesday following queries from Bursa Malaysia about several news reports by The Edge about the arrears, and the subsequent suspension of Zetrix and its subsidiary MyEG Sdn Bhd as JPJ collection agents, which Zetrix confirmed. (The Edge) TOPGLOV: Says ready for storms ahead as 4Q net profit jumps nearly five times Top Glove Corporation Bhd said it is confident of weathering headwinds ahead after earnings jumped nearly five times in the recently ended quarter, sending its shares higher. Net profit at the world’s largest natural rubber glove maker was RM157.63 million in the three months ended Aug 31, 2026 (4QFY2026), compared to RM34.83 million in the same quarter a year earlier. (The Edge) SAMAIDEN: Reveals RM238 mil contract value for LSS5+ solar project Renewable energy solutions provider Samaiden Group Bhd said its contracts to undertake works for a 99.99-megawatt (MW) Large Scale Solar 5+ (LSS5+) project are worth RM238 million. The group disclosed the contract value in a Bursa Malaysia filing on Tuesday, four days after announcing the contracts without revealing their value due to confidentiality restrictions. (The Edge) MSNIAGA: Wins two-year RM32.3m contract extension from Customs Dept Mesiniaga Bhd has won a RM32.3 million contract from the Royal Malaysian Customs Department (RMDC) for the maintenance and licence renewal of its MyGST System. The contract marks a continuation of the information technology product and service provider’s earlier MYGST system agreement with RMCD that first started in November 2023. (The Edge) SCIENTX: To acquire 503 acres in Johor for RM580 mil Scientex Bhd is acquiring 503 acres in Pulai, Johor, for RM580 million to boost the property developer’s land bank. The plan is to turn the 14 plots of land currently owned by the Lau family of Leong Hup International Bhd (KL:LHI) into mixed development, the company said in an exchange filing. (The Edge) DIALOG: JV bags onshore O&G concession in Thailand Dialog Group Bhd said its 50.01%-owned joint venture company has been awarded concession rights and operatorship for the L8/66 exploration block onshore Thailand. The joint venture company, Pan Orient Energy (Siam) Ltd (POES), was notified by the Thai government on Monday (Oct 5) that it had been awarded the concession following a joint bid with CanAsia Energy Corp in Thailand’s 25th Onshore Bid Round, according to Dialog's Bursa Malaysia filing on Tuesday. (The Edge) ELRIDGE: Invests RM45m to venture into activated carbon business Elridge Energy Holdings Bhd is investing RM45 million to venture into the manufacturing and the sale of activated carbon business for use across water treatment, industrial purification and related filtration. This marks Elridge's move further downstream from its existing palm kernel shell biomass operations. Its wholly owned subsidiary Insights Analytics Technologies Sdn Bhd accepted the letter of award from main contractor K J S Capital Sdn Bhd on Tuesday, the company said in a filing with Bursa Malaysia. title: 'GISBH Money Laundering Case to Proceed to Trial After Representation Rejected
body: 'SHAH ALAM (Oct 5): The Sessions Court here was informed on Monday that the representation submitted by the former chief executive officer (CEO) of GISB Holdings Sdn Bhd (GISBH) and three former company accountants to drop money laundering charges against them had been rejected. Following this, Deputy Public Prosecutor (DPP) Mohd Ashrof Adrin, who appeared alongside DPP Muhamad Ehsan Nasarudin, said the prosecution would proceed with the trial. “I regret to inform the court this morning that the prosecution wishes to state that the representation has been rejected and the prosecution will proceed with the trial. “We will be calling between 15 and 20 prosecution witnesses, and regarding the trial dates, I believe we will require six to eight days,” he said during case management proceedings before judge Datin Fatimah Zahari. The four accused are Nasiruddin Mohd Ali, 67, who faces 77 charges involving more than RM10 million; Hamimah Yakub, 74, facing 95 charges involving RM11.4 million; Asmat @ Asmanira Muhammad Ramly, 46, facing 68 charges involving RM4.7 million; and Mohd Khushairi Osman, 55, facing 91 charges involving nearly RM12 million. However, lawyer Datuk Rosli Kamaruddin, representing all four accused, informed the court that the defence intends to submit a new representation once the seized assets are officially returned to his clients. He said the new representation would, among other matters, address the possibility of resolving the case through a compound offer. “For the record, the previous representation did not address the issue of exploring a compound, so there may be a representation exploring this issue,” said Rosli, who was accompanied by lawyer Muhammad Zaim Rosli. He also requested the court to fix a case management date to determine the status of the new representation in January 2027. After hearing submissions from both parties, Fatimah fixed the trial for April 26 to 28, June 28 to 30 and July 6 to 8 next year, while the status of the second representation by all four accused will be heard on Jan 26. Meanwhile, Rosli also sought the court’s permission for the return of Nasiruddin’s passport to enable him to travel to Makkah. Nasiruddin, who appeared in court in a wheelchair, intends to meet his fourth wife, Ummu Mubaroqah Ashaari, 32, who is scheduled to undergo a Caesarean section this month. He said Muhammad Saleh Basharahil Hospital in Makkah had advised Nasiruddin to be present to provide consent for his wife’s surgery, as she is now full-term, although the exact date of the procedure has yet to be determined. Mohd Ashrof Adrin informed the court that the prosecution did not object to the application, subject to the conditions stipulated in the notice of application, including that the passport be returned to the court on or before Nov 10, 2026. The judge subsequently allowed the application subject to the stipulated conditions. On Sept 10, 2025, Nasiruddin and the three former company accountants pleaded not guilty at the Shah Alam Sessions Court to money laundering charges brought against them. The alleged offences were committed at bank branches in Selangor between 2020 and 2024 and involved transactions with various parties, including bank accounts belonging to GISBH Sdn Bhd, GISB Mart Sdn Bhd, GISB Travel and Tours Sdn Bhd and childcare centre companies. They were charged under Section 4(1)(b) of the Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001 (Act 613), punishable under Section 4(1) of the same Act. If convicted, an offender is liable to imprisonment for a term not exceeding 15 years and a fine of not less than five times the amount or value of the proceeds of unlawful activity at the time the offence was committed, or RM5 million, whichever is higher. title: 'A pay rise for only half the workforce
body: 'Lim Guan Eng was the first senior politicians to call for migrant workers in micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) to be exempt from the minimum wage and Employees Provident Fund (EPF) schemes. Now, the cabinet has exempted MSMEs from the upcoming minimum wage increase “for the time being”. The entrepreneur development and cooperatives minister, also from the DAP, announced the decision. Syabas (well done) on this remarkable ‘achievement’. Millions of workers in the sector have lost their right to a minimum wage increase. Official figures show about 48.7% of the country’s total employment are in MSMEs. That is 8.1 million people. Can Malaysia ever become a high-income nation with so many workers exempt from the minimum wake hike? We should also worry that wages will stay stagnant. Wage growth for 8.1 million workers will probably be held back. Two classes of workers Almost half of those workers will benefit from a higher minimum wage. The other half will, regrettably, be left at the mercy of their bosses for any wage reviews. This is discrimination in how we treat our workers. Even the government of the day never envisaged such injustice when it introduced the policy. The minimum wage was meant to set a floor for all workers. Since 2013, the government has never strayed from that core aim. - Sign up for Aliran's free daily email updates or weekly newsletters or both - Make a one-off donation to Persatuan Aliran Kesedaran Negara (ALIRAN), Maybank a/c 507246118995 or CIMB a/c 8004240948 - Make a regular pledge or periodic auto-donation to Aliran - Become an Aliran member Now, under the supposedly caring ‘Madani’ government, low-wage workers are being treated unfairly to favour one class of employers. It is a case of “harapkan pagar, pagar makan padi”. Some businesses will feel the impact of a higher minimum wage. The government should address their concerns case by case, rather than excluding the whole MSME sector. Denying close to 8.1m workers coverage under the new minimum wage increase is deeply unjust and morally wrong. We call on the prime minister to reverse the decision to exempt MSMEs from the upcoming minimum wage increase. title: 'Benign inflation keeps OPR outlook intact: CIMB Securities
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's inflation may remain benign despite firmer monthly price increases and rising food and electricity costs, according to CIMB Securities.   The research house said headline inflation rose to 1.9 per cent year-on-year (YoY) in August from 1.8 per cent in July, while core inflation eased to 1.7 per cent from 1.8 per cent, largely due to favourable base effects in information and communication.   However, both headline and core prices rose 0.3 per cent month-on-month (MoM), compared with no change in July, indicating firmer sequential price momentum.

title: 'IOI Marina View secures financing
body: 'SINGAPORE: IOI Marina View, a real estate developer, has secured an Islamic term financing facility worth SG$1.73 billion (US$1.35 billion) from DBS Bank, Maybank Singapore, OCBC and UOB, according to Allen & Gledhill, which acted as the transaction counsel to the banks. The facility will be used to finance IOI Marina View’s acquisition of investment holding company MVKimi.

title: 'Sebungkus nasi bahagi dua, duit poket hanya RM300
body: 'TUMPAT: “Setiap hari saya beli sebungkus nasi pada waktu tengah hari. Separuh saya simpan untuk makan malam sepanjang tiga minggu di Universiti Sains Malaysia (USM).” Demikian cerita Siti Noor Hidayatul Hidayah Sudin, 20, apabila ibu bapanya hanya mampu memberikan wang saku RM300 ketika menghantarnya ke USM di Pulau Pinang. Katanya, itu sahaja simpanan yang ada kerana telah membayar yuran pendaftaran sebanyak RM850 bagi mengikuti pengajian Sarjana Muda Pendidikan Khas. Katanya, yuran pengajian sebanyak RM1,232 belum dijelaskan meskipun sudah tiga minggu belajar di USM. “Jika ibu dapat pinjam dengan saudara-mara, dia akan kirim wang dalam masa terdekat untuk jelaskan yuran pengajian tersebut,” katanya menerusi panggilan video semasa kunjungan Ahli Majlis Presiden Gabungan Pelajar Melayu Semenanjung (GPMS), Che Muhammad Redzuan Jihad di rumahnya di Kampung Bunohan di sini. Siti Noor Hidayatul Hidayah berkata, dia rela mengikat perut kerana tidak mahu menyusahkan ibunya, Ramlah Abdul Rahman, 52, yang tidak dapat berjalan sejak empat tahun lalu selepas menjalani pembedahan kaki kiri akibat penyakit kencing manis. Katanya, demi membiayai pengajiannya, ibunya yang berkerusi roda gigih membuat kuih bersama bapanya, Sudin Matsan, 63. Bagi Ramlah, doanya sentiasa mengiringi Siti Noor Hidayatul Hidayah yang bercita-cita mahu menjadi seorang pendidik meskipun berdepan masalah kewangan. “Wang simpanan sudah habis digunakan untuk rawatan perubatan saya. “Walaupun menghadapi kekangan kewangan, saya tahu anak saya kuat semangat untuk menempuhnya,” katanya. Sementara itu, Che Muhammad Redzuan berkata, GPMS akan menyalurkan maklumat kepada Bahagian Hal Ehwal Pelajar (HEP) USM untuk membantu Siti Noor Hidayatul Hidayah termasuk wang saku, baki yuran dan sumbangan komputer riba. title: 'Three Banks Lose Buy Ratings as Bond Yields Rise; Hong Leong Names PBBANK Its 4Q Top Pick
body: 'Hong Leong Investment Bank analyst Raymond Ng Ing Yeow downgraded AMMB Holdings, CIMB Group Holdings and RHB Bank to “Hold” from “Buy” in a banking-sector review. He cut their target prices to RM6.70 from RM7.80, RM8.10 from RM8.70 and RM8.00 from RM9.50, respectively. In contrast, he upgraded Public Bank to “Buy” from “Hold” and raised its target price to RM5.30 from RM4.90, naming it his top banking pick for 4Q26. Raymond Ng Ing Yeow is ranked No.10 among 17 financial services analysts on StockTipRatings, based on data since 2023. He holds a 66% expert rating, with a 7% average return and a 56% success rate across stocks he covered over the one-year period following his calls. The changes come as the yield on 10-year Malaysian Government Securities rose to 3.94% on September 25 from 3.60% at end-June. Higher yields reduce the market value of bonds already held by banks, potentially weighing on treasury-related non-interest income before the benefit of reinvesting at higher yields emerges. Raymond said the immediate impact appears manageable, but repeated increases in yields could make earnings less predictable and limit further gains in bank valuations. Under his hypothetical 30-basis-point yield-rise scenario, the estimated gross mark-to-market impact for AMMB Holdings and Bank Islam Malaysia is equivalent to about 10% of their projected annual non-interest income, compared with 4.5% for CIMB Group Holdings and 3.2% for RHB Bank. Public Bank’s direct earnings sensitivity is lower at 1.3%. These are pre-tax estimates that exclude hedging and other offsets—not cuts to earnings forecasts. Raymond said the three downgrades reflect weaker visibility over non-interest income and a higher hurdle for bank-share valuations to rise further. He favours Public Bank for its exceptionally low impaired-loan ratio, resilient earnings and relatively limited direct earnings exposure to the bond-market sell-off, although its bond holdings could still affect book value. He maintained a “Neutral” sector view, noting that foreign investors sold a net RM1.3 billion of Malaysian banking shares between July 1 and September 25, while higher bond yields have made fixed-income investments more competitive. As of 2:09 p.m. on September 29, the Bursa Malaysia Financial Services index dropped 1% to 19,394.6 points.
